articles.title: Steiri of Boeotia - The Vampire 1953
articles.author: Αλέξανδρος.Β. Μπέλλος
articles.excerpt: The ethereal body of Loukas Kostakos has not yet dissolved. How metapsychists explain the shocking phenomenon in the village of Parnassida Steiri...

image.alt: Vampirism Phenomena in Steiri of Boeotia 1953

content.value: The ethereal body of Loukas Kostakos has not yet dissolved. How metapsychists explain the shocking phenomenon in the village of Parnassida Steiri.
Because the dead man speaks with his mother!

The shocking phenomena of the village of Steiri, which had alarmed the entire Parnassida region and recently the Athenian press, with all their overwhelming weight, place beyond any doubt the metapsychic views on the possibility of communication between the living and the dead and also the possibility of the dead manifesting spontaneously.

According to the opinion of reputable Metapsychic circles in Athens, the phenomena of Parnassida are of a purely metapsychic nature, and are caused by Loukas Kostakos who died a violent death. But let us see how events unfolded and what their metapsychic explanation is.

On May 23, 1952, at a quarry near Distomo, 17-year-old Loukas Kostakos was killed by a falling fir tree. Kostakos was from the nearby village of Steiri in Parnassida and, together with other fellow villagers, worked at the Barlos quarry, from which he would return to his village every evening by company car. On May 23, 1952, while he was working, a fir tree that other workers had cut down fell on his head without them calculating the distance separating them from him. That same evening the car brought Loukas dead to Steiri. The home of Kostakos and the entire village were plunged into mourning. The dead man was buried in the village cemetery, which is about five hundred meters away from it.

His grief-stricken mother mourned all day long, calling out for Loukas and continually invoking his soul, wishing to see him and speak with him. Time passed since then, when suddenly two months ago, Loukas Kostakos made his appearance first to his mother.

He told her that his death was not accidental. This fact, if true, justifies his persistent and varied manifestations. His mother hears him at night knocking on the front door, entering the house and walking through the rooms and the basement. One day she found the colt saddled in the stable — they had left it unsaddled and no one could get in there, since they kept it locked. Another day they found the colt in the basement with knotted knots in its rope's loop. These are a small part of the many strange things the people of Steiri recount.

Many nights they heard Loukas calling out the names of his relatives, visiting the homes of his fellow villagers and playing various pranks on them. He even went so far as to put a petticoat belonging to one of his fellow villagers — which she had lost — onto a mare.
All of this, however unbelievable it may seem, was verified as real.

The Society for Psychical Research, through its official representative Mr. Tanagras, categorically declares that the cause of the phenomena is the radioactivity emitted by psychically charged individuals, who through the ectoplasmatization of their unconscious, unknowingly perform all these tragic pranks.

In a most recent statement, Mr. Tanagras, being more cautious from a psychophysiological perspective, says that if all this is factual, then it is an extraordinary phenomenon of the greatest scientific importance. When asked whether a person who died a violent death can make their presence felt, he replied that such phenomena are observed in cases of people with terrible hatred, envy, great agitation, or excessive love for one person.
But for all of this to manifest, post-mortem consciousness must exist.

Precisely on this point, the Metapsychists fully agree: that Loukas Kostakos is neither a vampire, nor radioactivity, nor ectoplasmatic conjuring, but a post-mortem consciousness of existence which, due to violent death, carries an ethereal body that, when condensed, allows it to influence the physical matter of our world, causing these extraordinary phenomena. The metapsychic view holds that people who die violent deaths leave behind an ethereal body identical to the physical body, which must also decompose in order for the psychic body to remain undefiled and free. In those who die a natural death, this body decomposes a few hours after the burial of the corpse; however, for those who die a violent death, this ethereal shell of the soul remains for days, months, or even years, causing the dead to live a very earthly life, since they retain all their gross organs and earthly desires, which they try to satisfy in every way. In the case of Loukas Kostakos, something similar is happening.

He was neither a sinner, nor did he become a vampire, nor is this about ectoplasmic tricks, but rather about the pained soul of a young man who left our world unjustly, in the prime and vigor of his youth, and does not wish to abandon it until he receives satisfaction for the wrong done to him. As the Metapsychists also claim, every violent death is a great evil for the one who suffers it. Thus, Loukas Kostakos, imprisoned in an invisible body — certainly, but sufficiently material to be able to manifest in our world — wanders among the places he loved and suffered, until the body-like shell, as Plato called it, dissolves and he beholds the new world we call the Spiritual.
Until then, however, what must be done for the village to be freed from this nightmare?
This is known by the Union of Greek Metapsychists, which will take the indicated measures only when called upon for this purpose.

articles.title: The Mother-in-Law Showed the Bride Ghosts 1950
articles.excerpt: Drama of a mother who committed suicide to escape the torments of a mother-in-law who showed her ghosts.

image.alt: Shipwreck of Eleni Prinea, Kythira 1952

content.value: The drama of a mother who jumped from a ship and committed suicide to escape her torments.

Off the coast of Hydra, the body of Eleni Prinea, aged 27, was washed ashore yesterday and retrieved by fishermen. She had disappeared weeks earlier from the passenger vessel 'Eleni' while being transported under escort to Piraeus, where she was being taken to stand trial on suspicion of theft.

From the inquiries conducted by the deputy director of the Security Service of the Central Port Authority, Mr. Oikonomou, the following details emerged about the dramatic circumstances in which Prinea ended her life.

He learned that Prinea had taken her children, Adamantios and Stavroula, and her sister Olympia Psalida, aged 22, and had gone the previous June to spend the summer near her mother-in-law, who lived near the village of Agia Anastasia in Kythira. The first two months had passed harmoniously. At the beginning of August, however, Prinea's mother-in-law, due to inheritance matters, began treating her daughter-in-law in a very pressuring and harsh manner to force her to leave the village and return to Piraeus.

As testified by Olympia Psalida when interrogated by the Port Authority, her sister's mother-in-law had gone so far as to organize mysterious nocturnal stone-throwings at the windows of the room where Prinea stayed, and on many occasions ghosts had also appeared before Prinea.

As a result of these torments, Eleni Prinea's nervous system was so severely shaken that she suffered an intense nervous episode. She had reached the point of not recognizing her own children and on many occasions had tried to walk out into the streets half-dressed.

The drama reached its peak when, one day while she was being hosted by her sister Psalida in a house in the village, she was suddenly seized by a paroxysm and tried hastily to leave the room in which she had been isolated while gathering clothes that did not belong to her.

The commander of the station in the village of Agios Anastasios, to whom the incident of possible theft had been reported, charged Prinea with theft and sent her to Piraeus under gendarmerie escort to stand trial.

As a precautionary measure and to prevent a possible suicide by Prinea, who had shown such tendencies, she was handcuffed on the ship. Off the coast of Monemvasia, however, the escorting gendarme agreed to unshackle her for a short while, with the result that she disappeared and was unaccounted for until yesterday.
The husband of the suicide, Dimitris Prineas, when questioned by Mr. Oikonomou, testified that his wife was in perfect health when she departed for Kythira.

articles.title: 1949 - In Search of an Icon of the Virgin Mary Appearing in Dreams
articles.author: Εφημερίδα Ακρόπολις
articles.excerpt: The population of Konistres is searching for the icon of the Virgin Mary Chrysocheroa, following a vision of the young Despoina Georgopoulou.

image.alt: Icon of the Virgin Mary Chrysocheroa

content.value: IN SEARCH OF AN ICON OF THE VIRGIN MARY - A VILLAGE IN KYМИ IS IN TURMOIL. CHALKIS, 26. (From our correspondent).

The population of the town of Konistres in the Kymi district, gripped by intense religious emotion, is at this moment engaged in searches for an icon of the Virgin Mary Chrysocheroa, prompted by a dream seen a month ago by the young Despoina Georgopoulou.
According to the assurances of Georgopoulou, the Virgin Mary Chrysochera appeared to her in a dream and commanded her:
"Go to the property of Triantafyllakia Mposieph, near the Municipal School of Konistres. My icon is buried there. Tell everyone to go and dig and take it out."

Georgopoulou, terrified, did not sleep at all that night and the next day recounted her dream to the village priest, Papadogianni St. Stamatelis, who went to Kymi and reported the matter to His Eminence the Metropolitan of Chalcis, Mr. Ainian.
The latter, having examined the matter in detail and with ecclesiastical circles agreeing, gave permission for searches at the indicated location to find the icon.

This served as a rallying signal for the residents of the town of Konistres as well as of the other villages, who, led by the priest, gathered in groups, holding burning candles and with pickaxes and shovels, digging for the icon of the Virgin Mary Chrysochera.
It was frequently observed that the color of the candle flames changed to a deep red, mixed with blood-like hues. This was also noted by the police station commander of Konistres.
The latest event — the change of color in the flames of the candles — intensified the religious fervor of the residents, who were spending the night in the fields.
The searches continue under the observation of villagers as well as others from Chalkis.

articles.title: 1949 - Excavations for the Icon of the Virgin Mary Chrysochera
articles.author: Β. ΠΛΑΤΗΣ.
articles.excerpt: The excavations for the discovery of the icon of the Virgin Mary Chrysochera continue, with testimonies from priests and pilgrims from surrounding villages.

image.alt: Icon of the Virgin Mary Chrysochera

content.value: In Konistres, Euboea, excavations continue for the discovery of the Icon of the Virgin Mary Chrysochera. What His Eminence the Metropolitan of Karystia and the priests of the surrounding villages declared to our correspondent. Unprecedented influx of the faithful.

KONISTRES, 27. (From our correspondent.) — The excavations for the discovery of the icon of the Virgin Mary Chrysochera, also known as Tricherousa, which Despoina Georgopoulou repeatedly saw in her sleep and who told her:
"Go to the property of Triantafyllakia Billi below the municipal school of Konistres. I am buried there. Bring everyone to dig and take me out."

People of all classes and ages are streaming in with shovels and pickaxes from the surrounding villages of Monodri, Kytada, Andronianen, Tsairon, Kadon, Pasa, Kalimerianen, Pyrgos, Kymi, etc., continuing the excavation. The impressive Despoina Georgopoulou is constantly praying and insists that the icon will definitely be found, regardless of the sacrifices of fasting and fatigue, as she answers the thousands of questions of the pilgrims.

The gendarmes of the Konistres station, Th. Vournas and K. Denakis, reported: 'We too heard the bells of the village ringing and saw people running. — There are also others,' says Vournas, 'who, after the last apparition, saw the pit that had been dug and had filled with saltwater like holy water. Others saw icons in the water, others light, and they saw the icon of the Virgin Mary Chrysochera.'

Today, at the excavation site, the crowd of pilgrims found a piece of candle, the size of a bar of soap, seemingly very old and buried at a depth of about five meters. The crowd, apart from those working, literally rushed to the candle, which was divided into small pieces to make amulets.
This event further excited the interest of the pilgrims, who insist on finding the icon and are working feverishly.

I also spoke with the priests of the surrounding villages: Papadangelis Stamatelakis (Konistres), Papadimitrakis Kechris (Monodri), Papakostas Batziakou (Drimona) and Papanikolaos Siantos (Kalamarianon). All assured me that there is no reason to doubt the sincerity of what Despoina Georgopoulou saw.

His Eminence the Metropolitan of Karystia, Mr. Ananias, whom I met, declared to me: 'No one is permitted to doubt the faith and sincerity of what Georgopoulou says. I, together with priest Stamatelakis, officially placed the matter, in order for it to be conducted in agreement with the Holy Synod.'

articles.title: 1950 - Vision of the Virgin Mary in Limni, Euboea
articles.author: Εθνος
articles.excerpt: Testimonies of young people about an appearance of the Virgin Mary in Limni, Euboea, causing emotion and a flood of pilgrims to the site of 'Kanalakia'.

image.alt: The site 'Kanalakia' in Limni, Euboea, where the Virgin Mary is said to have appeared

content.value: As reported from Limni, Euboea, outside the town, at a distance of 500 meters and precisely at the site 'Kanalakia', where excavations were made fifteen years ago, following the revelations of Eirini Vasilaka, an icon of the Virgin Mary was offered. The young men Angelis Katsouras, Angelis Papageorgiou, V. Lagkadatos and Evangelos Souliotis were observing within the area of the archaeological excavations at a certain point, which was being marked by excavators.

According to their own information, a vision of the Virgin Mary appeared to the young men, who, holding a small red flag, walked a few steps toward the direction of the luminous barrier. Its brilliance was astounding, with the result that, at that moment, it blinded his sight and he fell to the ground unconscious.

At his cries and those of the other young men, who were terrified and became superstitious, many residents of Limni gathered on the spot, as well as the assiduous Nikodimos, who subsequently learned of this miracle.

But while the young men had not yet finished their account, those who had gathered saw, at a short distance from the spot, a great crowd holding an icon of the Mother of God, which, moving brilliantly, became luminous in the sky. This was also seen by many, who say it is the Virgin Mary the Liberatress. The icon was beautiful, holding a small red flag in her left hand while her right was extended in blessing. According to them, it was the same icon of the Virgin Mary of the Evangelistria of Tinos.
The Metropolitan of Chalcis, Grigorios, went to the site yesterday to verify the truth of the information from Limni.
Meanwhile, a great crowd is gathering at the site, venerating the vision and continuously chanting prayers.

articles.title: 1954 - The Discovery of the Icon of Saint Basil
articles.author: Ν. ΑΦΕΝΤΑΚΗΣ
articles.excerpt: The procession for the discovery of the icon of Saint Basil in the area of Oreos, guided by Maria Karagkouni and visions of sacred relics.

image.alt: Procession for the discovery of the icon of Saint Basil

content.value: ISTIAIA, May 17. (From our correspondent.) — Eight thousand and more inhabitants of Oreos and all the villages of Northern Euboea, led by the Metropolitan of Chalcis, Mr. Grigorios, attended a procession regarding the discovered icon, which was found following a vision of Maria Karagkouni, aged 45, from her village and mother of 5 children.

So far the following have been found: A very old small icon of the Virgin Mary of the Holy Table. Also the Holy Table itself with the inscription: 'The Holy Table was found through the inspiration of Saint Basil, and more will follow.'

Maria Karagkouni insists that the icon of Saint Basil and the Holy Chalice must be found, which she continually sees in visions. She herself reports that two years ago she had seen a white-haired elder who told her he was the founder of the church and that she must go to the home of priest Mbraila where the church is and pray.

After this vision, Karagkouni departed to the priest of her village, Sel. Chr. Christidis, who told her that a few sacred relics belonged to the home, among which Maria recognized the icon of Saint Basil.

The Metropolitan Mr. Grigorios, who will remain until next Thursday in Oreos, announced the founding of a women's Monastery to a 12-member committee elected by the villagers, for the protection and further investigation of the event of the discovery.
N. AFENTAKIS, Vradyni 17/5/1954

articles.description: Stone-Throwings by Entities - Notes of N. Politis
articles.excerpt: Traditions of demonic stone-throwings by nereids, spirits, vampires and other entities in various Greek regions.

content.value: Our people's traditions frequently mention stone-throwings carried out by demons. Thus, in Tradition no. 210, the Nereids throw stones from the whirlwind, and in Traditions no. 222-225, the Nereids chase and throw stones at people. In Tradition no. 041, a spirit; in Tradition no. 598, a ghost; in Tradition no. 440, an Arapas throws stones at ships. In Tradition no. 879, the Telonia are the stone-throwers; in Tradition no. 9225 the Good Luck Spirits; and in Traditions 944-945 vampires. As I note on page 869, the natural phenomenon may have given rise to such traditions. The belief in demonic stone-throwing is very widespread, and because of this, on many occasions, in various regions of Greece, cunning individuals have been found who exploited this conviction for their own purposes.

Usually the perpetrators of these acts are discovered and brought to justice for their misdeeds, but for a time the popular solution amuses the frightened superstitious masses, because the old belief is so deeply rooted that it should come as no surprise that this foolish practice is frequently repeated. We have all heard of such stone-throwings or have even been witnesses to them. Out of curiosity, I write from memory some examples known to me.

The incident having been reported to the 5th Police Department, Police Chief Mr. Maroulis went to the scene with some officers, but although he remained there for quite a long time, he was unable to determine where the stones were coming from. New calamities for our beleaguered planet are predicted by the Greek Metapsychists. Following the earthquakes of the Ionian Islands — which they claim was their own prediction — they now affirm that the Mediterranean will become the main center of a global geological upheaval.

In support of this prediction, they emphasize that the latest announcements from European Observatories regarding the earthquakes of the Ionian Islands state that these belong to the cycle of submarine earthquakes in Morocco, which pass through Sicily in all directions toward the Mediterranean.

articles.excerpt: Mysterious stone-throwing strikes a house in the Agia Varvara settlement.

image.alt: The house of Mrs. Leontiadou in Agia Varvara where the mysterious stone-throwing occurred

content.value: A house in Agia Varvara is being mysteriously stoned. The work of ghosts or a prank?
How the stone-throwing happens - what the police think - what Mr. Tanagras says

Do ghosts exist? An entire community — the residents next to the Pyritidopoieiou settlement of Agia Varvara — still swear that they do and moreover that they throw stones. The occasion is the stone-throwing during the past few nights at the house of Mrs. Venetia Leontiadou. A mysterious stone-throwing from invisible forces, as her neighbors believe. She herself is terrified, because she believes more than anything that it is ghosts. This is because she has no personal disputes with anyone that would lead her to attribute the stone-throwing to enemies.

The stones, as everyone says, fall on the house without it being visible beforehand where they come from. And they fall with a noise that spreads panic among all the neighbors, who now believe it is a haunted house.

To solve the mystery — if there is a mystery — the police station commander of Pyritidopoieiou, Mr. Koutsochera, posted gendarmerie guards at the house considered to be haunted, while ordering others to patrol the surrounding area. And the gendarmes noticed — or rather heard — stones falling on the house without being able to discover where they came from. They were not falling continuously, but at very sparse intervals. Every five minutes or more. And even last evening, at exactly 9:30 when we sought related information from the Pyritidopoieiou police station, they told us that the house of Mrs. Leontiadou was being stoned again at sparse intervals with both small and large stones.
The police's impression is that it is a prankster whom they are trying to discover and apprehend.
What Mr. Tanagras says
Mr. Tanagras, president of the Society for Psychical Research, whom we asked about this, told us:

"To begin with, stone-throwings observed in open spaces are not considered at all by science as potential telekinesis phenomena. This is because the possibility of staging cannot be excluded. The stone-throwing at the house in the Agia Varvara settlement could occupy the Society for Psychical Research if the stones were falling inside the house while doors and windows were closed. Furthermore, indications that it might involve telekinesis phenomena worthy of attention would be:"

"First, if the stones that fell were warm, and Second, if the same stones, however large they may be, cause no damage — as occurred in telekinesis phenomena where a stone weighing more than one okka fell on a gendarme's head without harming him. Like a piece of paper."
"So it's not about ghosts?"
"It seems not. Because none of the indications that science requires is present in the stone-throwing at the house in Agia Varvara."

articles.title: Mysterious Psychic Phenomena in a House in Agrinio - 1938
articles.excerpt: Mysterious psychic phenomena unsettle the residents of Agrinio, with muffled noises, voices, flashes and phosphorescent lights appearing in a house.

image.alt: The house in Agrinio where the mysterious phenomena were observed

content.value: Mysterious psychic phenomena unsettle the neighbors of a house.
Muffled noises, voices, flashes and phosphorescent lights terrifying the neighbors of a house in Agrinio. A peculiar hermit and his death. Mr. Tanagras will be summoned.
Messolonghi, January 10 (From our correspondent).
In Agrinio, the neighbors of a house in the city are in turmoil due to the mysterious psychic phenomena that have begun to appear in a strange and inexplicable manner.

Every night and during midday hours, in the aforementioned house, the neighbors hear mysterious noises, voices, inexplicable whistling sounds; peculiar flashes and phosphorescent lights are also sometimes reported, which cause terror in those fortunate enough to see them. Such is the terror of the house's neighbors that they now shut themselves indoors early, while the women pray and cross themselves exorcising the 'demonic.'

The said house belonged to the recently deceased Ioannis Kissavos, formerly publisher of a provincial newspaper in Agrinio, who in his last years had become obsessively involved with spiritualism, hypnotism and other psychic phenomena. Due to his pursuits he had become rather eccentric and lived as a hermit in a hut outside his house, where he lived seeing no one and conducting experiments.
How he died
This mysterious hermit had a premonition of his death, which occurred on November 15 of the previous year as follows:

One day exactly before his death he summoned the neighbors — something he was never in the habit of doing — and told them that the previous night, while he was awake, invisible mysterious forces lifted his body several meters off the floor and while he was floating in the void, let him fall down. Due to the fall, he injured himself seriously and felt that he was going to die. Indeed, the following day he passed away at the age of 75 and was buried in the Agrinio cemetery.
The phenomena

That same night of the burial, as his neighbors recount, the mysterious phenomena that cause such terror among the neighboring residents and which continue, began to be observed in the deceased's house. It should be noted that the following strange event was also observed.
Among the neighboring residents, a few quite courageous ones appeared, who decided one evening to enter the uninhabited house in order to ascertain the cause of the mysterious phenomena.

Indeed, they entered at night when the mysterious noises and voices were heard again, but they observed that after their entry and during the time they remained, the phenomena stopped completely. This, however, did not repeat on subsequent occasions when they entered the house.
In the course of these investigations, the following emerged:

The deceased Kissavos used certain objects daily, among them a chair, a table and an umbrella. The neighbors who were trying to ascertain what was happening removed these objects that Kissavos had used in particular and moved them to another house. And then it was paradoxically observed that the mysterious phenomena ceased to be observed at his house and began to occur in the house to which the objects had been moved.

All of this, quite inexplicable and mysterious, terrified the neighboring residents to such a degree that they are thinking of summoning to Agrinio the president of the Society for Psychical Research, Mr. Angelos Tanagras, to explain what it is about and restore calm to the neighborhood.

It should also be noted that another event has strongly aroused public interest in Agrinio regarding the phenomena and the entire case. The fact is that the deceased hermit had announced that treasures are hidden in another house in Agrinio, and it is believed that it is not unlikely he knew or guessed the locations of the treasures, since he was engaged in mysterious research.

articles.title: Solving an Arson Case Through Thought Transmission - 1930
articles.author: Ν. Αρχιμανδρίτου
articles.excerpt: A police officer extracts a confession of arson through a telepathic question during the interrogation of a burglar.

content.value: In Greece too we have cases where psychic phenomena have helped the Police in solving various cases.

I reported one such incident to the Society for Psychical Research, because it concerned a transmission of thought to me personally, through which the moral and physical perpetrators of an arson at a shop — which had occurred many years earlier — were revealed.

I will recount this incident to you: On November 7, 1930, as Commander of the 6th Security Department, I arrested the burglar Kyriakos Karakotas, aged 33, who within just 3 months had committed with his gang more than 100 burglaries at very central locations in Athens.
For the swift conclusion of all these cases I was forced to continue the interrogation day and night, with only brief interruptions.
Around midnight on November 12, 1930, I interrupted the interrogation briefly because I was very tired and remained in my office deep in thought, almost dozing in my chair.

Directly across from me, at a distance of one meter, sat the accused burglar Karakotas. At one moment I thought very intensely that Karakotas had committed arson, and automatically I turned toward him and asked him verbatim the following: 'Why did you set the fire, Karakotas?'
He immediately looked at me and in the most natural tone replied: 'Come on now... and I nearly burned the old woman too.'
He did not proceed to a more detailed revelation, however, because he realized that he had not until that moment confessed this act of his, which he had committed 4 years prior.

It was too late, however, because it was very easy for me, by searching the Archives, to find relevant evidence, and therefore, following my insistence, on the next day he approached me and revealed that on 15-11-1926, P… V…, aged 35, who maintained a shop on V… Street, had tasked him to set fire to it, promising generous compensation.
So that the fire would be considered accidental, he told him to place the incendiary materials in the dental office located above his shop.

When Karakotas went to set fire to the medical office, however, he noticed that an old woman was sleeping in an adjacent room, for whom he felt sorry because she would surely burn, and for this reason he set the fire not there but inside the shop.

All of this was confirmed as accurate; the relevant case file was found, and the Insurance Company that had paid out the insurance money was also notified, since the fire had at the time been considered accidental.
I have also made a relevant report about the discovery of this arson in the official Incidents Book of the 6th Security Branch.

articles.title: The Missing Person Case and Psychical Research in Criminology - 1934
articles.author: Ν. Αρχιμανδρίτου
articles.excerpt: Police investigation of an elderly man's disappearance with the help of an intuitive individual and an analysis of psychological approaches in criminology.

content.value: On June 27, 1934 at 8 in the morning, the disappearance of Konstantinos Sakkopoulos from the house of his daughter-in-law Efstathia, wife of Georgios Sakkopoulos, who lived at 16 Maroneias Street, was reported to the 2nd Police Department of Plaka.
The missing man was 90 years old and suffered from amnesia due to old age. The police searches for the elderly man yielded no result.

On July 2, that is 5 days after the disappearance, Efstathia Sakkopoulos together with Eleni Stathakopoulos, who were relatives of the elderly man, went to Miss Pavlatou, who was recognized by the Society for Psychical Research as an intuitive person.
Pavlatou, having placed herself in a state of auto-hypnosis, indicated that the missing person was at a house on 26 Veikou Street, where moreover she said she could see him.
Indeed, the elderly man was staying there due to an old acquaintance with the family, and had remained there until he was found, because he could not remember his home address.

We thus see that the use of psychic phenomena — or, to use the scientific term, the psychophysiological properties of the human being — contributed to serious cases that had attracted public attention, so as to dispel the dense darkness of mystery and bring truth to light.

This action in the specific cases was direct and exceptionally apparent. But nature willed that man's properties, which naturally manifest his inner world, should constitute the touchstone for every effort to improve society.

We thus see doctors practicing psychotherapy on patients with distorted perceptions, we hear daily the sermons of priests and participate in religious ceremonies and festivals, through which feelings are cultivated that contribute to the elevation of the human being as a personality.
We also submit to the measures taken by the state to alter the psychological state of those who rebel against justice and goodness.

If we accept the theories of criminologists, according to which criminals are patients of our society, then the question of using the psychophysiological properties of the individual for their improvement arises even more imperatively and is classified among the first measures to be implemented for this purpose.
In reality, however, no matter how much we try to soften the picture with philosophical veils, crime presents itself as a complex and not a simple phenomenon.

We cannot consider all criminals as patients of society, because the psychoanalysis of each individual will convince us that crime is the result of a hard struggle of their inner world with the causes that trigger irritation of the conscience and impulses toward evil.
It is true that for one category of offenders, crime constitutes a physiological need. It is not a pathological perversion, nor the influence of external or internal causes.
These were called 'born criminals' and were considered incapable of any improvement. For them, lifelong isolation is proposed as the only means of protecting society.
There is, however, another category of offenders: those for whom crime appears as a pathological phenomenon, as a kind of illness.
These individuals commit crimes not because they have an interest in or need for the proceeds of their misdeeds, but because they find in crime a perverted pleasure.
Depending on the form of the crime in which their perversion manifests itself, they are called pyromaniacs, kleptomaniacs, erotomaniacs, etc.
For them, the use of man's psychic properties is the only recommended means, as the fear of punishment produces no result.
Specifically, suggestion aimed at neutralizing the pathological impulse toward crime — whether in a state of wakefulness or under hypnosis — is absolutely effective.
Thus, kleptomaniacs can be suggested an aversion toward theft, pyromaniacs a revulsion toward fire, erotomaniacs a disgust toward sexual desires, and so on.
Besides these, another psychic phenomenon can help in the treatment and reformation of these pathological criminals: the inducing of amnesia for the past through hypnosis.
In this way the sinful past is erased and the person is given the possibility of a new life.
Beyond these categories, there are also those for whom crime is the result of free will. These are also the most numerous.
For them every offense is the result of the struggle of their inner strength against external impulses.
There is no exceptional circumstance or pathological damage; their intellect is balanced and equipped with sufficient resources to repel the impulse toward evil.
When, however, this balance is disturbed, then the culpability arises that the Penal Code punishes.

It is therefore necessary to strengthen the psychological state of these individuals, so that, even if at some point external impulses have prevailed over their inner strength, there is a way of correction and restoration of balance.
This can be achieved through the use of man's psychic properties, mainly through suggestion and auto-suggestion.
It is a fact, gentlemen, that we live in an era in which the human spirit explores in all directions of knowledge.
It has therefore turned its attention also toward the inner world of man, seeking the sources of these wonderful properties and trying to analyze them.

It found the thread of a complex and most delicate composition, an invisible mechanism with intense and impressive manifestations, and still struggles to determine the directions that must be given to this progress for the benefit of society.

Of course, every progress of the human spirit and of science, along with the good it brings, is accompanied by certain evils, intertwined with the new knowledge, as if a tragic law of nature exists that wants every progress to be followed by a corresponding drawback.
In the eternal struggle of good against evil, however, good cannot but prevail.
And we are fortunate that the Greek spirit, armed with the lens of science, did not lag in the investigation of psychophysiological phenomena.

We have often admired the progress made by the Greek Society for Psychical Research, which holds a prominent position in the international investigation of these phenomena, thanks to the activity and faith in the science of Psychophysiology of its wise and internationally renowned President, the esteemed and beloved Mr. Angelos Tanagras, to whom we wish God to grant eternal long life.

articles.title: Telekinetic Phenomena in Kallithea 1931
articles.excerpt: A 16-year-old boy in Kallithea involuntarily causes telekinetic phenomena: spontaneous fires, moving objects, and terror among the residents.

image.alt: Telekinetic Phenomena in Kallithea

content.value: A small boy who involuntarily ignites spontaneous fires and hurls various pieces of furniture. This is a telekinetic medium of great power. The bottles and knife that fly through the air — the terror of the residents.

Curious, admittedly, things that until recently were considered supernatural, began happening in a house in an Athenian suburb since the previous August. Completely inexplicable and astounding phenomena occur that, if they happened in some remote Greek village where people are superstitious, would be taken to be the appearance of strange ghosts or satanic forces capable of causing all these amazing things.

It was proven, however, after many investigations, that these are telekinetic phenomena caused by a very powerful telekinetic medium, who is none other than a small orphan child of only 16 years of age. He is young Michail Agrianitisb, orphaned from his mother, son of a carpenter, Mr. Dim. Agrianitis, who moreover has an illustrious descent, being the great-grandson of the fire-ship captain Pipinos.

He is a likable little boy, with lively and intelligent black eyes, who entering adolescence becomes, at certain moments, according to scientific explanations, a kind of radioactive body, and under the influence of subconscious impressions, radiates energy into his environment, which causes all these strange phenomena in his house, which is near the Agia Eleousa stop in Kallithea.
When the Phenomena Began

These astounding phenomena began precisely on August 15 of last year, but initially no great importance was attributed to them. Some phenomena that later turned out to be telekinetic date back to an even earlier period.

Initially, inexplicable scissor-cuttings of various garments that were hanging in different parts of the house were observed. That is, clothing was found cut with scissors that no one had touched, and this happened both during the day and at night, to the great surprise of the house's residents. Later, however, the destruction of various objects and the moving of furniture began to become so serious that everyone grew alarmed.

Among the first inexplicable phenomena was the following: One day the house's residents woke up and saw the flowers in the courtyard cut and thrown on the ground. Especially the flowers on the staircase had been slashed and not one was left intact. They thought, as was natural, that some bad neighbor or street children had cut the flowers. But the phenomena were repeated in a much more astounding manner this time.
Spontaneous Fires
Besides the inexplicable uprooting or cutting of flowers, fires began to ignite in various parts of the house, and indeed in places no outsider could approach to light a fire.

Initially a basket burned, which was in the basement of the house where young Michail lived, while moreover the medium's clothes were found inside the sink. Not much time passed and a second fire broke out on the bed of the child's aunt, Mrs. Anna Parisi...
This time too, at the edges of the basket, various half-burned magazines and newspapers were found...
At all these spontaneous fires, very close to the points where they were observed, many half-burned matches were also found...
Thus, after the spontaneous fires, stones began to fall on the house...
This continuous stone-throwing of the house, especially at night, made the residents anxious and they sought the intervention of the Police...
One night, young Michail's aunt was sleeping in the same room with him... and indeed found a stone in the middle of the floor.
From then on, the phenomena became even more alarming; damages to various clay vessels began to occur...
All of this might perhaps seem exaggerated but it is absolutely true because... the phenomena were repeated in the presence of credible witnesses...
Objects that Float
The truly astounding telekinetic phenomena continued in an even stranger manner.
Young Michail's aunt, to whom the phenomena are attributed, one day saw in amazement a metal knife...
Another day she saw a telescope lift itself from its place...
Even stranger is what happened with a bottle containing ouzo...
Another time again, a bottle full of wine shot by itself into the air...
An iron staircase railing was hurled by itself far away...
Later, even more damages began to occur. Destruction of foodstuffs began to happen...
What is happening? The behavior of the house's animals is also peculiar when these phenomena occur...
Initially, as we said, it was considered that these were 'satanic' phenomena and blessings were chanted...
Mr. Tanagras visited this house repeatedly... and concluded that these are telekinetic phenomena...

articles.excerpt: A villager from Kontovazaina committed suicide following telepathic and clairvoyant phenomena. Angelos Tanagras gave a scientific explanation.

image.alt: The Suicide of the Villager-Medium of Kontovazaina

content.value: A villager from Kontovazaina committed suicide after becoming a medium — he saw the Virgin Mary and Devils.
How he saw the village priest drinking in a coffee house — what he said about future earthquakes in Pylos — the explanation of the phenomena by Mr. Angelos Tanagras.

Astounding events of telepathy and clairvoyance occurred 3 days ago in the village of Raches, resulting in the tragic suicide of the man who was the medium of these most peculiar phenomena. The events that alarmed the villagers unfolded as follows:

In the village of Raches, which is 4 hours away from Kontovazaina, a villager named Georgios Dremitsikasb aged 20 had fallen ill with bronchopneumonia. The night before last, while his health was at a critical point, as if by magic he recovered and to the astonishment of his stepmother who was there and the other relatives, the moment he got up from bed he began recounting strange things.

He was telling them that at the moment when his illness was most intense, he saw on one side 40 demons and on the other the Virgin Mary weeping. The demons, who were very frightening in appearance, promised to give him 70 years of life and that they would bring his brother Stamatis, who was serving at a gendarmerie station in Tripoli, to play the clarinet for him — because his brother was indeed a formidable musician.
At the same time, they promised him wealth, happiness and a life of many pleasures.

From the other side, the Virgin Mary urged him not to accept the demons' offers because, within a few days, he would die. Instead, she urged him to bring the village priest, put on new clothes, and after wearing them and washing with unused soap, to go to the village church and deliver a speech from the pulpit, which the Virgin Mary herself would dictate to him.

The relatives of the patient who had suddenly recovered indeed remembered that the ill man had persistently asked for the village priest, but thinking it was simply the usual fever delirium, they kept telling him they didn't know where the priest was.

The patient then told them that the priest was at this moment at Malliароpoulos's coffee house drinking. To verify that he was indeed there, they ran to the coffee house the ill man had mentioned and indeed found the priest there drinking, and brought him to the house.

When the priest came, the ill man said to him: 'Priest, you are a sinner. You did this and that.' And he indeed recounted details of the clergyman's life, who was left astonished and left without agreeing to lead him to the church as requested.

When the priest left, a friend of the villager came, and because the ill man was shouting and saying that the demons would take his soul, he wanted to console him. The ill man then answered him angrily that a day before, his friend had sold his own wheat and had thrown away his sickle because it was not good. Both things had indeed happened. He himself also said that he had a fever of 38, and when they took his temperature, they saw that he indeed had that fever.

Faced with these phenomena, Dremitsikas's relatives were left astonished and did not know what to do. When night fell he told them that on August 31 earthquakes would occur and Pylos would be submerged, and after 27 years the Second Coming would take place.
During the night, however, the ill man escaped the attention of his relatives who were watching over him, took a knife and committed suicide, stabbing himself in the heart and abdominal area.
The president of the Society for Psychical Research, Mr. Angelos Tanagras, to whom we reported these events, gave the following explanation:

The suicidal villager, due to his illness and fever, had suffered a disruption of his psychophysical equilibrium. As a consequence, psychic phenomena of telepathy and clairvoyance developed, and this explains how he 'saw' the village priest at the coffee house where he was indeed, as he guessed, and that his friend threw away his sickle and that he had a fever of 38.

As for the rest, regarding demons and earthquakes in Pylos etc., these were nothing but hallucinations of his own, without any basis in truth. His suicide was the consequence of auto-suggestion, because he believed he had no more life, and based on this conviction chose to take his own life.

articles.title: The Haunted House of the Vavoula Neighborhood - The Devil Throws Stones 1906
articles.excerpt: In the Vavoula neighborhood of Athens, residents are terrified by mysterious noises and an elderly woman claims she saw the Devil throwing stones at a house.

image.alt: The Haunted House of the Vavoula Neighborhood - The Devil Throws Stones

content.value: The Vavoula neighborhood has been in turmoil since yesterday due to the mysterious noises heard in a house alongside Ralli-Areos Street.

We also went last night to hear the mysterious noises. The 'house with the ghosts,' as the neighbors call it, is quite large and newly built. It had been erected 2 years ago, and the residents had not had a moment's peace since they started living there.
Although the light rain prevented anyone from being in the street, some elderly people had gathered outside the door and were discussing the haunted house.
'I saw the thrice-cursed one with my own eyes!' said an elderly woman, making exorcism gestures. We approached and asked if we could listen too.
'Freely, my dears, why not?' 'Tell us then, Mrs. Pagona,' said a little old woman who was eager to listen.
'Well, the night before last, around midnight, while I was sleeping peacefully, I heard noises from the house across the way that immediately got me on my feet.'
'And then?'
'Wait now, I'm not educated enough to say it quickly, quickly.'
'So I got up from bed and went to the window to see what was happening.'
Here begins the tragic development of Pagona's vision.
'I raised my curtain and looked at the haunted house — and what did I see? The Devil was there... alive and kicking, on the roof tiles, throwing some black stones into the courtyard.'
'Mrs. Pagona,' we asked her, 'how did you see in the dark that the stones were black?'

Mrs. Pagona swallowed hard and then turned and told us: 'Come now, do you take me for a fool? The stones of hell are black. The moment I saw the Thrice-Cursed One I nearly fell down unconscious. The fright I got I will always remember and I cannot explain it to you. I pulled away from the window and lit the censer and said my prayers until morning. How could I close my eyes all night? I thought I could see him clearly before me.'

Mrs. Pagona's account ended. The fantastical little old woman, having completed her narrative, wrapped herself in her shawl and hurried inside her low little house, from whose windows we could see she cannot view the roof of the haunted house.

Tomorrow we will write to you about the causes of the mysterious noises in the haunted house, although we are certain that we will greatly displease our friend Mrs. Pagona, who will lose the opportunity to recount how she saw the Devil to other neighbors of hers.

articles.title: Thessaloniki - The Phenomena at the House in the Analipsis Neighborhood 1933
articles.excerpt: Strange phenomena at the Vogatzis villa on the corner of Delfon and Syndika Streets in Thessaloniki. Stone-throwings, noises and water cause terror among residents. Testimonies of a ghost or a trapped pickpocket.

image.alt: Thessaloniki - The phenomena at the house in the Analipsis neighborhood

content.value: Ghost or Pickpocket? The Analipsis neighborhood is in turmoil over the phenomena at the house on Delfon and Syndika Streets — stones continue to fall — military forces joined the guard and were stoned from above — suspicions mount that there is a pickpocket locked on the upper floor — the moving washtub and the running faucets — what Mrs. Nomikou says.

The Tachydromos, being the first and only newspaper that managed to inform its readers of the shocking details of the strange psychic phenomena observed at the intersection of Delfon and Syndika Streets, in the new villa of the settlement officer Vogatzis, was completely vindicated yesterday by the course of events, because yesterday too these phenomena continued, causing great panic among the residents of the lower floor and the neighbors.

The scene presented by the entire neighborhood can only be compared to the tragic days of an earthquake. The Vogatzis house, from morning until the next morning, is besieged by hundreds of neighboring residents, as well as residents from other neighborhoods who come to see the most peculiar phenomena.
These phenomena, exactly as they occurred, are narrated to us next by Mrs. Nomikou, wife of the chief of staff Mr. Nomikou, whose family lives on the lower floor and has been literally terrified.
But before we present the details recounted to us by the gracious lady, with the stamp of terror on her face, we give a picture of yesterday's situation and yesterday's phenomena.
The Haunted Villa

The Vogatzis villa is located near the end of Syndika Street and the back of the garden faces Syndika Square. It is a tall villa in a medieval style, with a roof surrounded by small battlements. This style, together with its ugly dark color, contributes more to the prejudice that it is haunted.
Thousands of Thessalonians visited this mysterious villa yesterday, while the neighbors have camped outside. A small coffee house directly opposite has been doing a roaring trade.
The villa is continually guarded by gendarmes, to whom since yesterday afternoon a few soldiers with a corporal were added, brought there by Colonel Nomikou.

The attention of all is turned toward the upper floor, which is uninhabited due to Mr. Vogatzis's absence in Aidipsos, and in which a mysterious visitor appears to be present, since, as we also wrote yesterday, mysterious footsteps and noises are heard, and furthermore, the small maidservant of the Nomikou family saw, as she assures us, at a window the wild face of a person who immediately disappeared.
The Mysterious Person
But who is the mysterious person? A ghost, a vampire, an evil spirit, or a simple thief who got locked inside and cannot get out?
But if it is a thief, what would this mysterious person have to gain by continuing to stone the lower floor? Escaping is impossible.
What is happening then? To this question, no explanation has so far been given, while the grand guignol-like phenomena began to repeat themselves from yesterday morning.

At 10:30 yesterday morning, the house guard, Mr. Bekos Athanasios, of the 1st Police Department, was urgently called to enter the Nomikou family's apartment, because under the apartment, in the basement, there was a strong smell of burning film and smoke.

The policeman went down to the basement but found no object on fire, and the smoke and smell immediately stopped. A little later, the family called the same policeman again because stones had fallen again from invisible hands.

In the afternoon, the stone-throwing was repeated, in the presence of police officers and journalists. This gave the opportunity for an important finding to be made. Until then, the starting point of the stone-throwings had been considered to be the fairly large garden extending to the back alley from the house. However, it was now noticed that the stones fall from above. It also seems that the throwing of the stones occurs from a small window next to the servants' staircase, whose pane had a fresh hole. Through this hole, the ethereal hand of a ghost, or the living hand of a criminal or madman, throws the stones toward the lower floor.
Why Don't They Open It
Our readers will wonder why the upper floor is not opened so that a search can be made and the agonizing mystery finally solved.

The reason is simple. The constitution prohibits breaking down the door in the family's absence. For this reason, the owner, Mr. Vogatzis, had been telephoned the day before yesterday to come from Aidipsos.

The latter, after requesting information by phone about why he was being asked to return, was also sent a supplementary message and it seems he will return. But even if he doesn't come, the police are determined to open the apartment to conduct a search, awaiting the view of the Prosecutor, who was informed of the case the day before yesterday.
What Mrs. Nomikou Says

Yesterday a reporter from the 'Tachydromos' spoke with Mrs. Nomikou. She is a very educated lady not to believe in ghosts. She is nonetheless agitated and thinks of her three little children, who have been panic-stricken and risk falling ill.

These phenomena, recounts Mrs. Nomikou, began at midday on Thursday. Some stones fell into the bathroom then. We thought children were throwing them. But there was no one in the street. At 4 in the afternoon, stones fell again and broke a pane in our bathroom. My husband who was resting woke up but found no one. He went as far as the washhouse, opened it, but found no one. We had the impression it was a prank. But the next day we searched the basement and the washhouse again and found traces of one barefoot person and one wearing shoes.

Also, the washtub had been moved from one corner to the other. This was evidence that someone had hidden in the washhouse the previous night. But naturally they had left. Then why did the phenomena continue? Because that same night Mr. Stafylopatis heard noise from the upper floor.
The following night, continues Mrs. Nomikou, stones began to fall again and one injured the maidservant Asimina in the leg.
Our maidservant saw yesterday afternoon (Sunday) a person at the window and ran terrified to tell us.
What She Imagines

'What can I tell you,' says Mrs. Nomikou, 'we don't know what to assume either and we don't have the headspace for detective reasoning. What we imagine — assuming of course it's not ghosts — is that a gang of criminals entered the house to rob the upper floor. One of them perhaps penetrated with a master key. The other two remained as guards.'

'Then why were they stoning you?' 'It seems the other one got locked upstairs. The others, to help him escape, started throwing stones in order to frighten us and make us leave. But since we're staying, this festival continues. But then again, I don't know... It could be ghosts, it could be telekinetic phenomena.'
What Is Believed

This view is quite logical and is also accepted by the 1st Police Department — that the phenomena could be caused by a person locked on the upper floor. With the difference that this person must be completely stupid if they think they can escape using the method of terrorizing residents and neighbors. So again we reach the conclusion that these are psychic phenomena of an 'unprecedented' nature, since the stone-throwing, noises etc. continue day and night.
The Maidservant as 'Sujet'
In any case, the 'sujet' of the telekinesis must be sought, and no other person than the 15-year-old maidservant of the Nomikou family, Asimenia Nikolara, can be the sujet of the phenomena.

But for these phenomena to occur and be caused by such a person, she must have a hysterical and peculiar nature for them to manifest. Which is clearly visible in her physiognomy, movements, and tone of voice. It is said that this young girl has at times also exhibited sleepwalking phenomena.
As for the phenomena, the young girl recounts exactly as her mistress does. 'Did you really see the ghost at the window?' we asked her.
'I saw him alive and in the flesh,' she answers. 'A pale and stocky man, with a mustache and disheveled hair.'
Other Phenomena

Since yesterday afternoon, the phenomena resumed at the mysterious villa. Among other phenomena, it was observed that a mysterious hand opened the faucet in the bathroom of the closed upper floor and abundant water had flooded the house. This water began to run down the staircase toward the lower floor. Last night, in the presence of police officers, several stones fell.
Mr. Vogatzis's Carpets
Yesterday, a very significant piece of information came to the police's knowledge, which may explain the reasons for the criminals' visit — if indeed it is criminals and not ghosts.

Everyone knows that in the closed apartment of Mr. Vogatzis there are silk carpets of great value. To obtain them, any criminal would be willing to risk their freedom and even play the part of a ghost.
Others Also Saw Him
Two civilians presented themselves at the 1st Police Department last night and stated that at the window of the house, they too saw a face for a moment and then it disappeared.

articles.title: Tatiana Karytidou - Saint and Witch - New Medium of Kilkis - Eidomeni 1938
articles.excerpt: The 19-year-old Tatiana Karytidou from Eidomeni causes wonder and fear for her telepathic and diagnostic abilities. The villagers consider her a saint or a witch — Angelos Tanagras summons her to Athens for study.

image.alt: Tatiana Karytidou - Saint and Witch, New Medium of Eidomeni

content.value: The 19-year-old daughter of the Greek-Serbian border who was revealed as a notable medium — villagers regard her as a saint and a witch — she is coming to Athens to visit Mr. Tanagras.

In the village of Eidomeni, that extreme station on the Greek-Serbian border, there is a 19-year-old named Tatiana Karytidou, who presents as a genuine medium. In the surrounding villages, a few months ago — from the time her fame began spreading about the astounding things she does — they regard her as a witch and exaggerate her wonderful deeds.

They say and spread astounding and improbable things, and the naïve who visit her leave crossing themselves, because they hear about various magic with which Karytidou can heal every type of illness, having visions and prophesying and making diagnoses of the internal organs of the human body.

Some regard her as a witch and others think there is an element of charlatanism in the affair, while most villagers take her for a saint. They say she communicates with Saint Modestos and with other spirits.

Certainly, however, if the tall tales and exaggerations are removed, Tatiana is an interesting type and medium. She has already departed for Athens where she will present herself to Mr. Tanagras for study.

The physician Mr. Adamantiou, who examined her, confirmed that Karytidou can, for example, close her eyes and, having a sick person before her, make a description of their illness. She finds what time exactly your pocket watch shows without seeing it of course, discovers lost objects, and objects in the house where she lives jump about when she has various thoughts.

She found a white tumor in the hand of a child while it was undergoing treatment of a different kind. This the people attributed to a miracle, and the villagers who see all these things are close to canonizing her.

The girls and all the women of the villages in general always surround her and ask to learn from Tatiana's spirits their fate and their sorrows. They constantly question her and have her converse with Saint Modestos and various other spirits, and when they see any strange thing around them they didn't expect, they attribute it to her.
Many times the chairs move on which the women are about to sit, and various objects fall that they are holding in their hands.

Many people consult her about illnesses. Tatiana takes hold of her head, closes her eyes, and after making great effort — which manifests as heavy sweat on her face — begins to describe all the internal organs of the body of the sick person she has before her. She thus finds the internal abnormality of the organism when one exists, and a physician can easily identify the type of illness, given that she can see and describe even the foreign bodies that may have developed inside the organism she is examining. This is how she discovered the white tumor in the child's hand we mentioned.
Her ability to understand various illnesses and see the internal organism of the human being spread her fame to the surrounding villages, and many villagers believe she is a saint.

The physician Mr. Adamantiou who examined her concluded that she, being seized by catalepsy, emits powerful radioactivity from her body. The diagnostic ability and the power of communication with spirits are attributed to the catalepsy, and the telekinetic phenomena to the radioactivity.

Tatiana Karytidou is a pale, thin young woman who noticed her telekinetic energy about a year ago inside her home, where she suddenly saw one day objects moving before her. At first she paid no attention and believed these were chance occurrences. When, however, the movements of furniture and objects began to occur more frequently, Tatiana reported the situation to her family, who began to monitor it. Thus the situation began spreading in her village and people from surrounding villages also began visiting to see her 'miracles.'

Within a few months all her telepathic and diagnostic abilities and the power of the radioactivity manifested, and the public now classified her among the 'saints' and also the witches, until at least the physician gave the explanation that this is a very powerful medium.
They themselves also advised Tatiana and her family to go to Athens and have Tatiana examined by Mr. Tanagras, which she did, having already departed to meet with him.
From Mr. Tanagras the actual extent of the new medium's real ability will be diagnosed.

articles.title: The Ghost of Alexander the Great - Mysterious Lights Above Ruins - Oritzari 1934
articles.excerpt: Mysterious lights at the ruins of Oritzari cause panic among the villagers, who believe they saw the ghost of Alexander the Great. Angelos Tanagras offers a natural explanation.

image.alt: Ghost of Alexander the Great - Mysterious Lights Above Ruins - Oritzari 1934

content.value: What is the most likely explanation of the legend about the appearance of the ghost of Alexander the Great.
What is happening in the village of Oritzari in Macedonia - Hoax or psychophysiological phenomenon - What Mr. Tanagras says.

According to information from our correspondent in Thessaloniki, for the past 20 days, throughout the entire region of Igoumenitsa, a story has been circulating — with various details each time — about the appearance of the ghost of Alexander the Great, torch in his right hand, at the ruins of the village of Oritzari. The villagers of Oritzari, more than anyone else, are preoccupied with the story of this ghost, terrorized, led by the priest and the schoolteacher, who also insist they saw — as did everyone — Alexander the Great roaming in the darkness with a torch in his hand.

Only the village corporal held a contrary opinion from the very beginning and even began questioning witnesses, suspecting that some prankster among the villagers had taken on the role of Alexander the Great for fun. In the meantime, however, the schoolteacher left in terror to Giannitsa, to report to the area inspector, who reprimanded her and sent her back to her village. The village priest, who is suspected of reinforcing the image of the ghost for tourism purposes in favour of his village, stubbornly insists that the ghost appears and calls on the sceptics of the surrounding villages to come and see.

Perhaps, therefore, with this persistence he has induced a kind of collective suggestion in the villagers, whom he will certainly have influenced with these stories as well as with tales of ghosts and spirits. Besides, it is well known how credulous villagers are, especially when it comes to mysteries. However, among the villagers of Oritzari there are also those who mock the priest and the others who claim to see the ghost. But the priest does not back down.
“I was not the first to see it for you to say it is my own fairy tale. On the contrary, the Vlachs came to my house and got me out of bed to run and see the ghost.”

“And did I see it? Something wonderful that I have never seen before. A luminous circle above the ruins of the ancient palace of Alexander the Great — it was sending off sparks and it was moving. I got scared and left. The shepherds also got scared and took to their heels. But the next night we went back out of curiosity. Now the light was like a half-moon that lit up and went out.”

Other villagers also confirm that they saw the complete ghost for a few moments. One in particular said he saw clearly, above the luminous point, a helmet of an ancient Macedonian warrior, and beneath it curls of blond hair.

And another, by the name of Delkos, recounts the events of the ghost as follows: “I had gone out before dawn above the village, to my field to plough. I saw a round light rising with many rays. I thought some shepherd had lit a fire. Suddenly I saw the light moving up and down, and finally coming towards me. At a distance of 50 metres I could make out something like a human figure. Out of fear, I turned back to the village.”

Similar are the accounts of all the others who believe in the appearance of the ghost. On account of these, the most curious of the villagers from the surrounding villages go to Oritzari. The correspondent of the Thessaloniki newspaper also went there in person, insisting that luminous and telekinetic phenomena are indeed occurring near the ruins, most likely due to some medium living near the spot.

Following this, a telegram was sent to the president of the Society for Psychical Research, Mr. Tanagras, asking him to study the phenomena. Mr. Tanagras replied that before going there, the phenomenon should be photographed if possible, in cooperation with the doctor of Oritzari or the physics teacher of the nearest village.
What Mr. Tanagras says.

In a statement made to our newspaper’s correspondent, Mr. Tanagras said that it is not a psychophysiological phenomenon, as will certainly be proven by the on-site investigation, and he is certain that the following has occurred: In this location there are marshes, as is well known, in which animals frequently drown. Their carcasses rot and it is natural for them to phosphoresce at night, emitting will-o’-the-wisp lights like the ‘cold flames’ in cemeteries. In the slightest breeze, these flames move left and right, up and down like fireflies, and this phenomenon is not difficult to create ghost legends among simple villagers.

articles.title: The Vampire Must Be Burned for the Village to Find Peace - Steiri 1953
articles.author: Θ. Δράκος
articles.excerpt: In Steiri, Boeotia, residents demand the exhumation and burning of a ‘vampire’. Angelos Tanagras offers psychophysiological explanations for the phenomena.

image.alt: Steiri 1953 – Discussions about a vampire at the coffee shop

content.value: The residents of Steiri demand the exhumation of Loukas Kostakos and the burning of his undecayed body - What Angelos Tanagras says about it.
At the village coffee shop in Steiri, around the stove, every day the sleep-deprived residents gather, terrified, with feverish anxiety in their eyes, discussing the events of the night.
“Did it appear again tonight?”
“Didn’t you hear it?”
“They say it visited old Kostakos’s house and tied the rope in knots around the mule’s neck…”
“You forgot that it hit the old man badly. It grabbed him by the hair and was dragging him to take him away…”
“Where will this evil end, people? What will become of us? What explanation is there for its appearance? Will it keep frightening us every night?”
All these people rightly face this terrible nightmare.
“What do you say?” they ask me. “How do you think we can get out of this? There is a scientific explanation, people. But first I would like each of you to tell me what happened to you.”
And the people begin to recount their troubles.
First to speak is Mr. N. Gkovis. Then Simos Matthaios, G. Marinos and many others. Each one recounts a characteristic visit by the vampire.
“But are there vampires, people?” I ask them. “Do you have the impression that they exist?” “Of course they exist,” they tell me with certainty.
“Many years ago, in Tsamali at Petromagoula they exhumed one and burned him. That is how the entire region was freed from his appearances.”

“That is what we are asking for now too,” the Community Secretary Mr. Lagos tells me. “To carry out an exhumation to see what is happening. If Loukas Kostakos has decomposed, then we can believe something else is happening. Now, whatever you tell us, our minds cannot accept it.”
And indeed, how could all these events that trouble them every night fit in their minds?
“And why don’t you carry out this exhumation? Have you not asked for permission from the Prosecutor of Livadeia, Mr. Benovkas?”

“The Community President submitted a document outlining the events occurring in the village. From then on it is a matter for the prosecutor to decide. And indeed this document was forwarded, by order of the prosecutor, to the Gendarmerie Station of Distomo. And the latter, as I was informed, is about to proceed to Steiri and conduct a related inquiry to get to the bottom of it.”
But can anyone get to the bottom of such things? Here is what has happened, strangely:

The TEA commander, when he heard about the strange telekinetic phenomena occurring in Steiri, decided to reassure the village. And one night four TEA members were guarding the house of Sirgianni and watching to see what was happening.

“We took our weapons,” one of them told me, “and sat outside the door, on the threshold. Suddenly, in the middle of the night, we heard someone knocking at the front door of the house. We immediately jumped up towards the stairs and shone our electric torches at that spot. However, we saw no person and naturally, we were completely dumbfounded.”

But they are not the only ones who are dumbfounded in this case. Before continuing our investigation, however, we wanted to see what exactly the views of the President of the Society for Psychical Research, Mr. Angelos Tanagras, are.
What Mr. Tanagras says
Mr. Tanagras has observed many similar cases in the past. And indeed he explains to us in every detail what exactly must have happened in the village of Steiri.

“On another occasion,” Mr. Tanagras told me, “there had been a great commotion about a vampire that was appearing at the coffee shop by the walls of Mesolonghi. There, truly, many astonishing events were occurring for simple villagers. Those among the café regulars who had the courage and could follow this spectacle would see glasses full of water moving on their own from the counter and being served at the tables. Turkish delights coming to customers before they had even ordered them.”

Tables and covers of jars were also opening and moving. These events were undeniable. And people started confidently discussing that the café owner had murdered someone and that person had become a vampire and was doing all these astonishing things to take revenge and announce his presence.

The café owner was in a very bad state, people began to look upon him with suspicion. Everyone was in turmoil. The rumour of the Mesolonghi vampire had spread everywhere. People were not sleeping in their homes and were frightened. I investigated this case and found that all these phenomena were being caused by a young employee of the coffee shop named Vourvachis. The owner rushed to dismiss him. These phenomena immediately stopped. But Vourvachis was hired as an employee at another coffee shop and then the Turkish delights started leaving on their own and the glasses of water started being served to customers on their own there too. Naturally they dismissed him from there as well. Then the phenomena began to be observed in his own home. Eventually, after some time, Vourvachis stopped having this ability.
The explanation of the phenomenon is not difficult. There is what is called psychic radioactivity. A thousand causes can create similar phenomena, like those happening in Steiri.
“Can a person be in a house and cause similar phenomena from far away? In the dwelling of another family?”

Certainly. All these phenomena can be explained. But what is striking is the calling out of names, the footsteps heard clearly and the moaning. If these are real and not a matter of autosuggestion, then it is an exceptional phenomenon of the greatest scientific significance.
“Have there been cases where various signs like those that occurred in the village of Steiri were observed in animals? The knotting of the horse’s halter?”
Certainly. A characteristic case has been documented. A horse’s mane was found braided in small plaits while the animal was locked in the stable.
“Can a person who died a violent death make their presence felt?”
Such phenomena are observed in cases of people with intense hatred, with great and powerful agitation, with excessive love for a person…
