articles.title: Drapetsona - The Wonder-Working Girl with Supernatural Telekinetic Abilities 1937
articles.excerpt: In the ‘Vatikiotika’ quarter of Drapetsona, young Anna Kouvoutsakis causes a stir with telekinesis phenomena. Angelos Tanagras offers a scientific interpretation and announces he will study them on site.

image.alt: Drapetsona 1937 – Telekinetic phenomena in Vatikiotika

content.value: The truly strange telekinetic phenomena we wrote about in yesterday’s ‘Akropolis’ have been observed for several days in the ‘Vatikiotika’ quarter of Drapetsona and for yet another day became the topic of the day for the residents of the Piraeus district.

Some attributed them to ‘evil spirits’ and others to the ‘mysterious electromagnetic energy of man’. In any case, there were also a few who did not believe the phenomena were real and wanted to see them for themselves as ‘doubting Thomases’.

The household of Kouvoutsakis was flooded and besieged by this last category. All day long it was surrounded by curious onlookers and the family could not find any peace. The object of all this attention was the Koukoutsakis daughter, Anna, a very modest and likeable girl, who may well be an exceptional medium.

The first manifestations of these telekinetic abilities in the young woman were observed, as we were informed, on the night of the previous Sunday, shortly after her return home after a two-hour walk with her parents.

When Anna entered the house that afternoon, the window panes began to creak and various light objects began to move. These phenomena terrified the young woman and her parents and they all rushed out in panic from the house into the yard. There, after remaining for a short while and recovering from the initial shock, they went back into the house whereupon the phenomena continued. That is, the panes began to creak again and various objects began to move. When Anna approached the fireplace and tried to light it with small kindling, these began to be flung in all directions around the room. These phenomena, which in the meantime had become known from the accounts of the family members, caused a stir among the residents of the small neighbourhood. From that day on, every evening pieces of tiles and stones began leaving the roof and falling noisily into the yard.

The stoning raised suspicions that it might be caused by unknown persons and for 2 nights, two officers from the port authority stayed up together with many neighbours, without any of them being able to detect a suspicious individual who could be stoning the house.

The day before yesterday morning another astonishing phenomenon occurred. Anna went into the yard to get the brazier and bring it to the kitchen, and as soon as she picked it up the burning coals began to be flung in various directions. Filled with terror she began to cry out and dropped the brazier from her hands. Everyone then was seized with awe, and because those close to Anna could not explain the phenomena, a priest was called to ‘drive the evil spirits from the house’ and restore calm to their souls.
But, unfortunately, they did not find peace. The house continues to be disrupted by these astonishing phenomena, and the curious keep streaming there continuously, asking for related information.
We saw them yesterday when we arrived at their little house and heard from their own lips their ‘troubles’.
“We have been living in this house for three years and nothing like this had ever happened to us. Now we ourselves do not know how to explain these strange things.”
Anna, this likeable girl to whom telekinetic abilities are attributed, also expressed her own amazement ‘at what has been going on in her house since last Sunday’.

“These things that happen in our house every so often are very strange. Sometimes the furniture creaks, sometimes small objects move and sometimes stones fall in the yard. The strangest thing is that when I leave the house calm returns, as if I am the cause of these things happening. But it breaks my mind why it did not happen before, and I think specialists must come and examine and find the cause.”
The same is said by all the neighbours, on whom the manifestation of the telekinetic phenomena has made an exceptional impression.
What Mr. Tanagras says

These phenomena used to be attributed to supernatural causes, to vampires etc. For 50 years now, however, science has undertaken to investigate them and it has been established that they are caused by a person living in the house, whose psychophysical balance has been disturbed. Causes of this condition can be powerful psychic shocks due to deaths, painful operations, or due to the development of puberty in both sexes, or the end of a woman’s fertile period at around 45 years of age. Because it has been proven that ‘libido’ exerts a tremendous influence on these phenomena.

As a consequence of this psychic shock and psychic turmoil, which instead of erupting as neurasthenia or psychasthenia or a nervous breakdown, erupts as some emission of energy from the body, as if the human organism is transformed into a radioactive body. It emits what is called telekinetic energy, from which the telekinetic phenomena originate. These phenomena consist of the movement of objects, the opening of closed doors, banging, sounds of footsteps, disappearances of objects, stonings with warm stones, which fall without causing blows or damage. These phenomena terrify the neighbours because they have a sense as if they have their own consciousness.

An electrical discharge can suddenly knock a glass of water over, but it cannot carry it without the water spilling. Therefore, at first glance it seems logical to believe that such phenomena are manifestations of the dead who are trying in this way to announce their presence. Today however, as we said, it has been proven that the cause of the phenomena is one of the residents. Because as soon as this person is identified as the source of the phenomena and is removed from the house to a great distance, the phenomena stop. Additionally, since these phenomena are produced unconsciously and do not depend on the will, it is not possible to reproduce them experimentally.
Fortunately, an exception to this rule is the amateur medium, unique in the world, Kleio Georgiou, whose telekinetic power is such that it can be demonstrated experimentally at any moment.

Last year similar phenomena were observed at the house of General Diamantopoulos, where the cause of the phenomena was his young servant, and damage of many thousands of drachmas had been caused. Samples of these damaged garments are kept at the offices of the Society for Psychical Research. Correspondingly, regarding the telekinetic phenomena in Piraeus, the source of the phenomena must be identified and removed from the house. The phenomena will stop immediately.
Mr. Tanagras stated that he will most probably go to Drapetsona this morning to study the telekinetic phenomena occurring there on site.

articles.title: The Mysterious Phenomena of the Messolonghi Gate - Spiritualist Explanation - 1927
articles.excerpt: In Messolonghi, the coffee shop outside the Fortress Gate is disrupted by telekinetic phenomena and the appearance of a ‘spirit’. Angelos Tanagras travels on site for investigation.

image.alt: Mysterious phenomena at the Messolonghi Gate (1927)

content.value: For the past fortnight the town of Messolonghi has been in turmoil. At the coffee shop of Mr. Dimitrios Baltas, managed by Mr. Stefanis Georgiou and located outside the Fortress Gate, regular bangs are heard; tables, chairs, jars of sweets and Turkish delights are shaken and fall; the water jug is overturned and glasses topple, and astonishing events take place.

Most astonishing of all is the appearance of a ‘spirit’ in the form of a child and its disappearance before eight residents of Messolonghi, among them Mr. Ioannis Bempantakis, president of the Gardeners’ Association, Mr. Christos Papatheos, secretary of the Municipality, and Mr. Kon. Papoutsopoylos.

According to explanations given at spiritualist sessions, the phenomena are produced by the spirit of the deceased retired consul Somakis and of an Armenian prisoner of war who was murdered in 1913 by a Messolonghi soldier, a crime unknown until today. According to spiritualism, the crime was committed in order to steal the precious jewellery that the prisoner had with him.

The spirits are creating this noise because their common grave was destroyed. The Armenian was buried, according to the account, inside the family tomb of Somakis by his murderer on the night of the crime. Later, however, when the iron railings of the monument were sold, that spot was dug up.

According to the ‘confession’ of the spirit of the late Georgios Chronis, many things have happened at that particular spot in the past, and there was once an old church; with these signs the world is called ‘to repent’. The existence of life beyond the grave and the existence of the Divine Majesty are also attested.
The phenomena, always according to spiritualism, will continue even more intensely, if the damaged monument is not restored and ecclesiastical prayers are not read at the spot.
The events also attracted the attention of the Society for Psychical Research in Athens. For this purpose Mr. Tanagras arrived, to whom all the incidents were confirmed.
Mr. Tanagras examined the young employee of the coffee shop, Christos Vourvachis or Rapanania, believing that the phenomena are due to a property possessed by certain individuals, known as mediums.

Mr. Tanagras conducted hypnosis experiments on the nurse of the Chatzi-Kostas Hospital, Elisavet Moschaki, in the presence of the scientists Mr. Gr. Papageorgiou, Pantelis Kotsis, K. Skotaras, Sozontas Midioni (pharmacist) etc.
Mr. Tanagras will remain for a few days in order to personally witness the phenomena and, if possible, photograph them.
Source: Newspaper STEREA ELLAS, 09.01.1927 – ‘Mysterious Phenomena of Messolonghi’.

articles.title: Supernatural Phenomena in the Psyrri Quarter 1908
articles.excerpt: In the Psyrri quarter, the lawyer and music teacher A. Tsiknopoulos claims that the walls of his room filled with icon paintings and 'supernatural' representations, with eyewitnesses and descriptions of moving figures.

image.alt: Supernatural Phenomena in the Psyrri Quarter (1908)

content.value: The Mysterious Room - Symbolic Representations and Heads of Saints
Saints have entered a house in Athens.

While Mr. Tsiknopoulos, a resident of one of the rooms in this house, was sleeping one evening, he saw in his sleep an unknown deity, who informed him that his room would soon fill with icon paintings. Mr. Tsiknopoulos did not believe the dream and continued sleeping and studying in his room, unsuspecting.

One evening, however, he saw a cross forming on his wall. A few days later he saw the head of an old man, then many others, and now, when the sun sets and the man tries to close his eyes, the room fills with saints, with heads of old men and animals mentioned in the Holy Scriptures.

Any other person would have gone mad. The occupant of the room, however, maintained absolute silence about the matter at first, and when he saw that the uninvited strangers had no intention of vacating his walls, he called other people to verify the thing.

A painter, another neighbour and many journalists went there in person and confirmed that Mr. Tsiknopoulos was seeing things and not chimeras. The walls of his room were filled with strange iconographies. One old man in particular with a white beard - a saint himself - had only one eye and with the other he observed, without blinking, Mr. Tsiknopoulos.

The painter confirms that he had one eye because he was painted in profile. In any case, however, any person would have difficulty sleeping if on the wall of his room 'spent the night' an old man with one eye. And it is not the first time that these white-bearded old men make such indiscrete appearances.

The Athenians remember very well that on another occasion an old man with a white beard and two eyes - this one was more courteous - appeared one October morning on the back of a Greek scholar and even forced him to be photographed with him. That old man was identified as a French scholar and gave rise to malicious tongues saying that, out of jealousy, he was bothering his Greek colleague.

But that is an old story. Since then in Athens these ghosts have made many 'conquests'. In a house in Metaxourgeio, unknown ghosts stoned a residence day after day, so that not a single pane of glass remained intact. Then these ghosts changed their field of action and went to a grocery store and left not a penny in the shopkeeper's drawer. And finally, a few days ago, they thought it was permitted for them all to spend the night together in a room, where it is questionable whether even Mr. Tsiknopoulos alone fits.

The afflicted occupant of the Psyrri room confirms that these old men are saints, who prefer the walls of his room to paradise. And I am certain that these saints will not leave easily from there. Mr. Tsiknopoulos will spend money in vain on liturgies and prayers. Sooner or later, though, he should whitewash his room walls.

In the nature of things and in the general economy of Creation, phenomena appear many times that, however sceptical one may be, however much one is inclined towards investigation rather than blind conviction, one cannot but recognise as supernatural. So inexplicable are they and so far do they exceed the rules that govern Creation.
Such appears to be the phenomenon being observed at the house of the very well-known and well-educated lawyer and music teacher, Mr. A. Tsiknopoulos.

Wishing, however, to remain within the realm of positive facts, we shall record here, word for word, the communications of Mr. Tsiknopoulos and the other reliable persons who saw and perceived these supernatural appearances. For it is precisely 'appearances' that are involved, along with the names of the eyewitnesses and the images of the supernatural representations that appeared.
THE MYSTERIOUS DWELLING

The house is two-storied, very old, and consists of five rooms, two of which look out onto Aesopou Street, while the other three together with the kitchen look out onto the small courtyard of the house.

A narrow entrance leads the visitor to a wooden, aged and worm-eaten staircase, by which one communicates with the upper floor, where the well-known lawyer and music teacher Mr. Andreas Tsiknopoulos resides with his family.

The room in which, as we were informed, faint figures of various saints, icon-painting representations and many symbols are visible on the walls, looks out through two windows towards the direction of the street and is overflowing with books, bookcases, icons, tables and seats.
The room in general has the appearance of being in the middle of moving, since the tenant, in order to move out on 1 September, has turned everything upside down.
Two windows and two doors are on the sides of the room, which, besides the rest of its contents, also has a bed on which Mr. Tsiknopoulos sleeps.
This house belongs to the landowner Mr. Th. Kritsis and it seems it was built on top of an ancient church, though it is unknown which one.
THE SUPERNATURAL REPRESENTATIONS
To anyone who visits this mysterious room, initially nothing supernatural presents itself that would lead him to disturbing thoughts and make him want to examine the phenomenon.
With careful examination, however, he immediately perceives that irregular brushstrokes of paint colour various representations and symbols.

It must be admitted that the representations and depictions, especially of heads and crosses, are not perceived by the examiner unless he is first guided by Mr. Tsiknopoulos, who, as he told us, has for some time been engaged in the precise identification of each icon-painting figure or symbol through an appropriate combination.

On all four walls of the room, painted in light lilac colour which has been covered by an ochre colouration, with careful observation and the guidance of the resident one can make out irregular, sometimes vivid and sometimes faint frescoes depicting various forms.
In empty spaces, light shades form large crosses and other symbols.
CLEARLY VISIBLE REPRESENTATIONS
Among other things, we also observed some somewhat more vivid representations.

A head of an old man with a serene expression, with light shadings, with eyes that have a sorrowful expression, with a completely undefined nose, a small moustache and a hand-span beard, appears to most likely represent Saint Anthony.
Contributing to the more vivid representation of this figure are also some slight, yet clearly visible, indentations and protrusions of the wall surface.

At a very short distance on the same wall there appears a phenomenon worthy of serious dispute: a more recent coat of ochre, such that the new colouring forms a representation that cannot easily be defined.
With careful observation, lines are discernible that form garments, more likely of an ancient Greek woman, that is a goddess or a priestly figure.
HOW THE PHENOMENON IS EXPLAINED
This phenomenon - which is real and can serve as a basis for anyone who wishes to dispute the existence of the other icon paintings - is explained by Mr. Tsiknopoulos as follows:
“This represents, he told us, the goddess Athena, most likely, or some other figure.
“You should bear in mind that the representations, which I first discerned and then many icon painters and others, are aimed at the symbolism of our Church and the ancient Greek nation.
“Above Athena you will discern a hand and another symbol that expresses the substance of the Holy Spirit, under whose immediate guidance certain persons prophesied and spoke on certain occasions.”

Not wishing to recount things as seen and examined by Mr. Tsiknopoulos - a distinguished lawyer and deep expert in our religion - whose lengthy interview we publish tomorrow, we continue with the recording of the representations and icon-painting images, which were perceived by the reporter who visited the apparently mysterious room.

This phenomenon does not surprise us, because due to the different rays of light entering the room from four open points during the day, light-and-shadow effects are created depending on the position of the viewer, which, if the viewer wishes to represent them in his imagination, form a complete jumble of images: they 'say' much, but accurately and completely render nothing.

The brushstrokes of successive coats of paint left disorder and remnants of colours, some of which became more vivid and others almost invisible. In some places lighter colours appear with small shaded spots, in others curved lines, in others scratchings of the wall, so that the whole, combined, presents a symbolism that only at night can be examined more accurately.
A MOVING HAND
- The threatening serpent
- The incense

On the wall facing Aesopou Street, and precisely in the middle of the two windows, an icon-painting representation is discernible, only slightly visible but vivid, which puts even the most sceptical person in serious thought about its supernatural appearance and substance.

Far from any commentary and from the slightest doubt, which can give rise to either contempt or scepticism towards divine and supernatural events, as well as from any suspicious explanation, we shall content ourselves only with the reproduction of the symbol, which we perceived with our own eyes.

This symbol consists of a fairly clearly visible hand of a saint, below which protrudes the head of a serpent with a threatening expression, which the incense of a censer located a little lower sometimes makes to grimace angrily.

To nocturnal visitors, among whom were the icon painter Mr. Vlassopoylos and Anastasios Korbetis, this symbol made the following impression: the hand, as many times as the head of the serpent moved towards it, withdrew, as if it were oscillating and as if it were shrinking.
This clearly visible 'cinematic' scene was followed by some light shadings, coming from the censer, which made the icon-painting representation somewhat fainter and darker.

In tomorrow's issue we shall publish extensive interviews with serious persons who were eyewitnesses of these supernatural events and will shed considerable light on the explanation of the phenomenon.

Expert icon painters, summoned by us and Mr. Tsiknopoulos, painted several of the supernatural forms and other icon-painting representations appearing there, photo-engraved images of which we shall publish tomorrow.
Also, for the explanation of the phenomenon, we shall publish the opinion of an eminent theologian.
THE IMAGE OF THE VIRGIN MARY
- A supernatural expression
- Eyes that weep

Continuing the description of the clearly visible forms depicted on the walls of the mysterious room, we shall attempt to describe a vivid image that represents the Virgin Mary holding Jesus Christ in her arms.
The image is large in size, with fairly vivid features on the faces of both figures, which are characterised by intense expressiveness.

The eyes of the Mother of God, with their deep shadowed brows, have a mournful and sorrowful expression, contrasted with the smiling and innocent gaze of the divine child, who rests calmly in her arms.

What is paradoxical and truly hard to explain is that the more one pays attention to the face of this image, the more details one discerns - to the point of believing oneself that, if one is not in the presence of a supernatural phenomenon, one is at least experiencing a terrible optical illusion.

In those who examined this image carefully, among them scientists and many sceptics regarding such events, slight movements of the eyes of the Virgin Mary were also perceived, from which, at certain moments - as the eyewitnesses confirm - tears appeared to flow.
Paradoxical is also the sideways inclination of the eyes of the Virgin Mary towards the eyes of Christ, which do not appear to move.

This image is the most vivid of all the others. Towards it will be directed the attention of anyone who wishes to offer a faithful and precise explanation, for it presents, in contrast to almost all the others, a certain regularity from a proportional point of view.
WHAT MR. TSIKNOPOULOS SAYS
Closing today's information, we add also the opinion of Mr. Tsiknopoulos regarding these supernatural phenomena:

“So many things have happened to me,” Mr. Tsiknopoulos told us, “in which I discern a sequence and the closest connection, that I hesitate to recount them to you, lest I be taken for a mystical and divinely inspired man. I am, however, fully convinced, and I base this on indisputable spiritual phenomena, that I will shortly be in a position to make known things which, with difficulty admittedly, but yet at some point, a man can see clearly in moments that are few in his life, but strong enough to convince him that he is not dreaming or delirious.”
Source: Newspaper CHRONOS, 25 August 1908, p. 2.

articles.title: A Living Mummy in Kolchiko - A Monster with Golden Eyes and Claws 1932
articles.excerpt: In the area of Lagkadas, villagers and a field guard describe nocturnal appearances of a 'living mummy' with a golden appearance, that attacks and disappears. The residents are considering calling Angelos Tanagras and Dr. Delivoria.

image.alt: A living mummy in the area of Lagkadas (1932)

content.value: The nocturnal visit received by a field guard - The terrorisation of the residents
THESSALONIKI, 28 August (from our correspondent) - Mysteries are reported from the area of Lagkadas, and specifically from the village of Bogya of Kolchiko.

Unprecedented mysteries, almost incredible, despite all their plausible interpretations. It is no longer a matter of ghosts, nor of vampires, nor of a village medium who has suddenly manifested telomagnetic properties.

And Mr. Tanagras, we assume, will find himself in a difficult position to determine exactly what is involved, from the following faithful description of the strange events, as recounted by the affected villagers.
First appearance

In the Macedonian countryside at this time of year, most residents sleep outdoors. While the exhausted farmworkers rest, someone keeps vigil for their safety and that of their labours: the field guard.

In this case the field guard was and is Nikolaos Karamegdanis. It was around midnight on one of the last nights and the field guard, lying at the base of an olive tree, was 'half-sleeping', as the common expression goes, when he heard light footsteps behind him. Initially he thought it was a small nocturnal animal and, half-raising his body, he heard the footsteps approaching.
He then noticed that the sound was coming from behind a dense thicket of brambles. Somewhat alarmed, he prepared his weapon and tried to get up.
A golden shadow

But he stayed on the spot, because he clearly discerned passing behind the thicket a human shadow, tall, enormous, golden in the moonlight. Then the shadow disappeared. The field guard hesitated to believe what he saw.
Uncertain, he still sat with the weapon in his hand, until he shuddered again, hearing the sound of footsteps. He could not hold back a cry of terror and amazement.
The living mummy
Before him stood, in the moonlight, a grimacing mummy.

The unfortunate Karamegdanis was paralysed with terror. With widened eyes he observed the monstrous creature, which was wrapped in a kind of yellow shroud, had a head resembling that of a jackal, with short hair and a golden face. The hands and feet of the mummy were dark red. A heavy odour emanated from this human monster.
The mummy takes the weapon

The mummy took a step towards the half-dead field guard and, bending down, took his weapon. It examined it curiously and then let it fall. And when it wanted to pull also the night covering of the field guard, the latter, gathering his strength, leapt up and began to run shouting:
- Help, help, a living mummy!
Behind him a laugh was heard, like a quiet mooing...

And these things occurred that night. The field guard, running with all his strength and shouting, fell among the farmers Dimitrios and Nikolaos Moschos. They revived him and heard his account with astonishment.
All three then proceeded armed to the place of the appearance, but found nothing other than the weapon and the covering of the field guard. The mummy had disappeared.

The following night, however, while Dimitrios Moschos and a friend were sleeping near a rock that belonged to an old mine, they were awakened by a strange noise. They thought that someone was trying to lift a heavy stone.

They raised their weapons and, in great fear, discerned under the strong glare of the full moon the living mummy, exactly as the field guard had described it, emerging from the shadow of the rock, enormous, golden, majestic.
They shoot, in vain

At one point they fired at the monster one, two times. In vain. The mummy stood still, but suffered not the slightest. It observed with some surprise, opening its gleaming eyes, the two farmers. Then it set off and, pushing aside a dense thicket of rushes, made an enormous leap and found itself between the two villagers.

The moment was indescribable. Dimitrios Moschos and his companion, now moved by the instinct of self-preservation, tried, closing their eyes, to push the monster away. But they felt the hard and iron-like fingers of the wild phenomenon on their necks. They were shaking all over with spasms and would certainly have suffered a heart attack, if the monster had not let them go and, with quick steps, had not disappeared behind the rock.
The two villagers, taking courage, followed it, but found nothing and heard nothing until morning.
What is it all about?

All these are facts reported through letters and accounts of the villagers of the Kolchiko area. No one can dispute the credibility of the good and brave farmers, just as no one can explain what mystery is about to be revealed with this strange appearance of the living mummy.
Many claim it is a wild man.
This is ruled out, because the monster is completely shaven and dressed in almost new fabric.

Others say it may be a humanoid ape. It is well known however that such apes do not exist in Greece and generally in Europe, nor has a travelling circus ever passed through Kolchiko, so that one could accept that one of its apes escaped and is wandering about.
All the accounts and facts indicate that it is a mummy of a tall, sinewy, majestic man, who thinks and acts with complete rationality.
What on earth is happening?

The residents of Kolchiko are considering addressing the president of the Society for Psychical Research and asking him to come in person and examine the phenomenon. They even requested that the president of the Society for Psychical Research be accompanied by Dr. Delivoria, who is considered one of the best mediums.

articles.title: A Student with a Radiant and Luminous Body - 1934
articles.excerpt: A Law student is said to light electric bulbs with his hands. The rare psychophysiological phenomenon is examined by the Society for Psychical Research and causes puzzlement among physicists.

image.alt: A student with a radiant and luminous body (1934)

content.value: - He lights electric bulbs with his hands.
- How the phenomenon is explained.

ATHENS, 17 May (from our correspondent). Among the various and most numerous psychophysiological phenomena that have from time to time disrupted various cities of Greece and which superstition has surrounded with imaginary veils and attributed to malevolent 'spirits', there is added today the most astonishing, unique in our country and extremely rare even throughout the rest of the world.

The Law student Mr. Panagiotis Kouloumvakis, 25 years old, from Kardamyli in Laconia, produces sparks inside electric bulbs as soon as he holds them for some time in his palms or rubs them. This astonishing phenomenon was also proven experimentally two evenings ago at the 'Society for Psychical Research'.

During the experiment, when Mr. Kouloumvakis began to rub the bulb in his palm in the darkness, very clear sparks, luminous arcs and broken luminous lines like miniature lightning bolts were outlined, for a period of approximately two minutes.

At any moment he is able to produce sparks in a bulb or make it radiate. The same phenomena are observed when he rubs the bulb against any part of his body. After sufficient rubbing, simple contact with that point of the body suffices for a continuous radiation to appear.

He first observed the phenomenon three years ago, when he was serving as a soldier in the field artillery, near the mansion of the Duchess of Plakentia, seconded to the meteorological service of the regiment.

During the replacement of a broken bulb in the laboratory, the bulb lit up on its own in his hands. The same happened with a second bulb, an event which caused terror among his colleagues, who attributed the phenomenon to ghosts.

He himself, out of curiosity, began to experiment and found that the phenomenon recurred. He even reached the point of always keeping a small bulb in his pocket, which he lit with his hands in the dark to illuminate and unlock the place where they slept.

Professor Mr. Athanasiadis, whom he approached, rejected the possibility of electrical transmission from the human body, explaining that sparks in a bulb require a voltage of approximately 6,000 volts.

The study of the phenomenon was entrusted to specialist physicists of the University and to Mr. Dasiou, director of the State Chemistry Laboratory. If the electrical nature of the phenomenon is excluded, only then will the Society for Psychical Research examine it.

Similar, though less intense, phenomena have also been observed at sessions with mediums. Recently in France, the body of Miss Mareno was radiating, mainly in the area of the heart, during the crises of her illness.

articles.title: The Astonishing Phenomena of Divri - 1929
articles.author: Κ. Φαλτάιτς
articles.excerpt: Large stones that do not strike and fires that burn clothes but not human flesh convulse Divri. The case of Eftychia Pantazi causes upheaval throughout the village.

image.alt: The astonishing phenomena of Divri (1929)

content.value: In psychical and spiritualist phenomena, it is good for those observing them to draw up a report. People who do not follow the phenomena are sceptical, however much those who happened to be present as witnesses may tell them. Written documents, however, are more convincing and more reliable.
It is difficult to establish facts and it is not easy to refute written records. For this reason, reports of psychical phenomena should always be drawn up on the spot by those who observed them.
When did the phenomena cease
The phenomena occurring with Eftychia Pantazi appear to have ceased, had she decided to change her place of residence.
'How are we to do that, though,' she herself and her husband say. 'We are poor people. We cannot leave our village and uproot ourselves. We can only do so for a few days.'

And indeed: Eftychia Pantazi had left Divri for one week and gone to the neighbouring village 'Logki'. She stayed at the house of a relative of hers for one week. Throughout this entire period neither stones fell nor did automatic fires light.
Eftychia felt better within herself. The headaches, dizziness and vomiting had diminished.

'I was saying that the trouble had passed,' Eftychia recounts to us, 'and after one week we returned back again to Divri. But the first night I stayed here, the same things again. The place seems to carry it.'
Both Eftychia and her husband accept our advice to leave Divri again. They do not know where to go, however, because they cannot keep burdening acquaintances in the surrounding villages.
Nor is it easy to go down to Lamia, because life there is expensive and, as they had already written to us, the people are poor.
Eftychia Pantazi and her husband, with their so sincere and guileless physiognomy, predispose the visitor very favourably, who shares their distress and sorrow.
It is not only Eftychia and her husband who are suffering. The whole village is in turmoil and saddened by what is happening, which no one can dismiss.

'Our Community is poor,' says the President of Divri, Mr. Kourathanas. 'If the Community had the financial means, we would give a credit for them to leave the village for a while. But the Community is very poor.'
The automatic flames
Eftychia Pantazi showed us not one or two but numerous burned clothes. Her own dresses have been burned, head scarves, linen covers and a kilim rug.
'Nine times so far fires have broken out,' she says. 'One was on my child, the others on the clothes I wear and the others on the clothes we cover ourselves with.'
'It is something like an electric switch turning. Together with the stones, fires also light. Only the stones fall daily, while the fires do not light every day.'
'I don't feel any burning. My clothes catch fire and turn to ash, but I suffer nothing.'
'This is called in science acaia,' Mr. Garthikis explains. 'That is, a fire that does not burn flesh and burns only clothes and objects.'
We leave Divri
Our journalistic mission has ended. With sorrow we bid farewell to the village and its residents.
'Do you think the stones and fires will cease?' they ask us. 'We believe so. As long as you leave the village.'
The phenomena continue to occur and whoever comes to Divri can perceive them.
Author: K. Faltaits - I Vradhyni, 02.09.1929

articles.title: Mysterious Stoning of a House in Zakynthos - 1933
articles.excerpt: Continuous and mysterious stoning of a house in Orthonies, Zakynthos causes upheaval in the village. The police intervene and Angelos Tanagras gives instructions for investigating the phenomenon.

image.alt: Mysterious stoning of a house in Orthonies, Zakynthos (1933)

content.value: Following the Makrisia events in Olympia, new telekinetic phenomena again in Zakynthos. The village of Orthonies on the beautiful island has been in turmoil for a week.

Every night, after 11 o'clock and until well past midnight, one of the village's houses, the house of Dionysios Pylarinos, is the target of a fierce, continuous and mysterious barrage of stones, which puts the residents and the whole village on their feet.

The first manifestation of the phenomenon occurred more than a week ago. The family of the villager Dion. Pylarinos had gone to bed early and around eleven at night, while all its members were sleeping deeply, they were awakened in terror by the sharp sounds that were heard in rapid succession on the roof tiles of the house.
'Ghosts,' as even the naive villagers of any other village would say, who explain phenomena of a similar nature through the tradition of spirits and vampires.

And immediately they all got up and came outside in terror. Their first task was to check whether someone was on the roof tiles of the house playing a prank, perhaps a fellow-villager who wanted to amuse them, even in this peculiar way.
A night outdoors
In the meantime, it should be noted, the phenomena continued and on the roof tiles of the mysterious house small stones were rolling, continuously producing the same sounds.
From the noise and anxiety of the house's residents, many neighbours also woke up and everyone gathered around the house, where for a long time they followed the demonic sounds.
Everyone found a cause to associate with these ghosts. Some said that a certain old man who was killed many years ago a little further from the house had turned into a vampire.
Others that many years ago a woman had died in this house and they had allowed the house cat to jump over the coffin on the night of the lamentation.
And others that the residents of the house were excommunicated by Saint Dionysios, patron saint of the island, because they had not gone to worship him for many years.
A little later the stoning stopped, but the residents of the stoned house spent the night outside.
The police are called

When morning came, the whole village learned of the matter and the villagers gathered on the spot and tried to explain which of their fellow-villagers had become a vampire and was now throwing the stones.
Under the protection of daylight the frightened residents went back inside the house and waited anxiously until the following evening.
But the following evening too the stoning continued, the sounds on the tiles and the rain of stones below the house, and the residents were forced to go out into the street again with greater fear.
The police were notified and sent a force with an officer. Despite the vigilant supervision, the phenomena continued for many more days.
The Prefect addressed a letter to the president of the Society for Psychical Research, Mr. Tanagras, asking him to visit Zakynthos and explain the phenomenon.
Mr. Tanagras replied that he could not travel to Zakynthos and recommended that the temperature of the stones be monitored at the time they fall.
If the stones are warm, this means that there is a person with telekinetic properties in the house and they must be removed. If they are cold, then it is a hoax.
The villagers of Orthonies picked up stones that were falling and found them somewhat warm.
Whether this is due to prejudice or a real phenomenon remains unknown.
The cause of the phenomenon remains unexplained and continues to trouble the villagers.
Akropolis, 15.09.1933, p. 2

articles.title: The White Ghost of the Depo Appears Every Night - 1933
articles.author: Α. Θνητός
articles.excerpt: Residents' accounts of the appearance of a white spectre at the Depo of Thessaloniki. The phenomenon causes upheaval, religious fervour and hypotheses about a miracle.

image.alt: The white ghost of the Depo in Thessaloniki (1933)

content.value: The White Ghost of the Depo Appears Every Night
The strange appearances of a white spectre - What those who saw it say - It resembles a white-robed priest praying - The ghost had appeared before 30 years ago

The appearance of any saint or even ghost among us mortals has always been of exceptional interest to the general public. The human soul is always restless about the hereafter and always seeks to learn news from it, details about life there and whatever else it can grasp in its restlessness about life after death.

And, when no one can achieve this, one gets into a stir and crosses oneself before an event that possibly only took place in one's imagination. And one lights candles and prays, makes processions and supplications on bended knee and spends whole nights in penitence, trembling and imploring the messenger from the 'other world' for the salvation of one's soul.
And it happened!

In any case, the miracle happened. In the excitable imagination of simple people or in reality, it does not matter. The fact is one: that an entire neighbourhood near the Depo is in turmoil. After more than thirty years of rest and obscurity, there appeared a saint according to some, a priest dressed all in white according to others, a white spectre according to yet others.
The appearance
This story took place in the Depo neighbourhood and specifically on Thermopylae Street. The accounts come from eyewitnesses.
It was a Friday afternoon, at the hour of vespers. The ten-year-old Takis Anagnostopoulos saw on the rocks of the small hill a priest dressed in white, sitting and praying.
Frightened, he called his mother, but the spectre had disappeared. Since then, as he says, many others have seen it.
The little one's miracle
Yannakis Titilas, the son of a fisherman, also saw the spectre at night, standing upright, appearing to pray and then disappearing like smoke.
He claimed that the spectre entered an opening beneath a rock, a hole that - according to the children - had not existed before.
The fulfilled appointment

The carpenter Periklis Karagkounidis, a resident of the area, stated that he had been waiting for the appearance for eleven years. The spectre appeared at midnight, took the form of a man with raised hands and disappeared when a rooster crowed.
After the disappearance, the area was filled with the scent of incense.
And... a little treasure

Crowds of people flock to the spot. Some to see the place, others to light a candle and others in the hope of finding treasure, as it is said that in the past there was a monastery that was destroyed by an earthquake.
The stones of the spot are not ordinary; it seems they had been worn by water for many years, possibly from the sea.
Regardless of what the spade might reveal, the mystery remains.
Author: A. Thnytos
Source: Makedonia, 12.06.1933, p. 1

articles.title: Communication with the Dead - Spiritualism - Psychophysiology 1935 (Part 3)
articles.author: Φώτος Γιοφύλλης
articles.excerpt: Interview with Angelos Tanagras on whether communication with the dead is possible, the position of psychophysiology and his disagreement with spiritualism.

image.alt: Communication with the Dead and Psychophysiology 1935

content.value: By what means does science attempt to achieve communication with the dead?
Continuing our interview with Mr. A. Tanagras, we asked him if he believes that communication between the living and the dead is possible.

Mr. Tanagras replied that he does not believe the human soul after death retains memory of the actions and events of earthly life. He does believe, however, that the psychical 'self' remains immortal after the dissolution of the material body.
In his view, the loss of memory after death constitutes a form of rest for the soul, as the retention of memories would be equivalent to eternal psychical punishment.
The soul, according to him, remains immaterial, immortal and self-sufficient, with no further interest in human events and the actions of the living.
Research in Europe
Researchers in psychophysiology do not consider communication between the souls of the dead and the living to be proven, in contrast to spiritualists who accept it fully.
Spiritualist researchers exist throughout the world, among them important scientists and intellectuals such as Kardec, Flammarion, Conan Doyle and Lombroso.
Spiritualism in Greece
In Greece, spiritualist activity appeared intensely from 1890, centred in Athens with experiments at the house of the poet Georgios Souris.
Important personalities of the era, poets, doctors, politicians and journalists, participated in experiments and studies of spiritualism.
And in the provinces
Spiritualist activity spread to the provinces as well, with centres such as Patras and Corfu, where associations were founded and experiments carried out.
In Patras, the Society for Psychical Research, under Professor Georgios Floudas, conducted experiments of great scientific significance based on psychophysiology.

articles.title: Reportage: Telekinetic Phenomena in Vythos, Kozani - 1952
articles.author: Ακρόπολις
articles.excerpt: Telekinetic phenomena in Vythos, Kozani in 1952: objects that move, icons that fall and villagers who speak of vampirism after the death of the grandmother.

content.value: Vythos, a small picturesque village near Pentalofos, has been in turmoil for fifty consecutive days because of the mysterious telekinetic phenomena occurring at the house of the widow Stavroula Magiani. The photoreporter and exclusive correspondent of 'Akropolis', Mr. Thomas Ionas, is the only journalist who, despite the bad weather, managed to reach the snow-covered Vythos, conduct an on-site investigation and photograph the main persons of this startling story.

These mysterious phenomena appeared at the house of the widow Magiani, who lived with her three daughters: Dialekto, aged 20, Zacharoula, aged 17, and Dimitra, aged 14. Five to six days after the death of their grandmother, that is, of Stavroula's mother, who died at the age of 92, the inexplicable began.

Stavroula and her three daughters, who were sleeping together in one of the three adjoining rooms of the house, discovered one morning in astonishment that all the objects in the other rooms had been moved. And they had been moved in a certain order, as if caring hands had moved them.
The icon of the Virgin Mary, which was high up in the icon stand, was found on the ground. And in front of it was found lit, as always, the small poor oil lamp, made from a white cup.

The clothes, all the clothes, were found spread neatly on the floor with their hangers. The blankets, the chairs, everything, absolutely everything, had changed position. The possibility of someone entering through the window was excluded, since the windows had iron bars.
The women were frightened, but said nothing to anyone. They thought it wise to double-lock themselves in their room the next night. They stayed awake out of fear that night.
Without any noise being heard, without any window or door opening, the next morning the objects - which they had put back in their places - were found as on the previous morning.

Lady Stavroula was frightened and ran to her brother.
- So and so.
- Nonsense.
- But it is as I say.
- I'll come with you tonight to see who is doing this.
Her brother stayed the whole night in the house. At dawn they all found that the same things had happened again. Pale with fear, they could not give a rational explanation.

The explanation was given later by the village:
- Grandma Chaido has turned into a vampire.
- That's it.
- There's no other explanation.

It was decided that two or three would stay in the 'haunted' house to dispel the legend. At their head went the village president himself, Giannis Gasparis. But in the morning they all came out pale-faced and admitted that something supernatural was happening.

The village priest, Mr. Michalis Lytras, was called, who performed exorcisms and read prayers at the house and at the grave of the late Chaido. It is said that the phenomena stopped temporarily, but soon started again.
The photoreporter of 'Akropolis' put the objects back in their places, photographed them and then photographed them again in the position they took on their own.

The Gendarmerie Headquarters, taking as its occasion the fact that the Thasos police hastened to bring to trial the persons at whose house telekinetic phenomena manifested, addressed a circular recommending the prevention in the future of similar actions, which present the Gendarmerie as behind the times with regard to contemporary scientific research.

articles.title: Communication with the Dead – Spiritualism – Psychophysiology 1935 (Part 4) – Haunted Patras
articles.author: Fotos Giofyllis
articles.excerpt: Astounding experiments in Patras and an account of the ghost of the Rio fortress. The director of the Patras Society for Psychical Research, Mr. G. Floudas, describes medium experiments and the appearance of Diovahnesco.

image.alt: Haunted Patras and the Rio fortress – 1935

content.value: Communication with the Dead – Spiritualism – Psychophysiology 1935 (Part 4) – Haunted Patras
The astounding scientific experiments… — What was revealed in Patras — The Rio fortress is haunted — The appearance of the spirit of master builder Dovanesco

The experiments of psychical science in Patras are considered significant. Regarding these, the director of the Patras Society for Psychical Research communicates the following exceptionally interesting points:
– Psychical science confirms the truth concerning the existence and immortality of the soul.

The press has often reported on telekinetic phenomena — the movement, that is the displacement of objects without contact or physical force. Such phenomena were observed in Messolonghi in 1928, in the Patras suburb of Zarouhleika in 1930, and last year in Makrysia, Elis, to mention only our own region. They were studied by Societies for Psychical Research.

Innumerable phenomena are cited, among others, by the famous Italian professor Lombroso, who admits that he had previously been an opponent of such notions concerning the soul and spirits, maintaining that every force is a property of matter and every thought a property of the brain, and he would scoff whenever he heard of moving tables.

But, after observing numerous psychic phenomena, he accepted the existence of an immaterial intelligent force which persists after death, visiting persons and places of its earthly life of its own volition — phenomena of haunted houses — or at the invocation of the living.
Accordingly, Mr. G. Floudas, director of Psychical Research in Patras, disagrees with Mr. A. Tanagras, since he accepts the communication of souls after death with those still living.
THE GHOST OF RIO

– For example, Mr. Floudas continues, concerning the Rio fortress, it has circulated since time immemorial that it is haunted. Many who were prisoners during the time the fortress served as a prison for serious offenders recount a host of anecdotes about a Black Man who would appear enormous, with large sunken eyes, long bony hands and a club, and would strike or attempt to strangle the inmates.
At other times, they recount, he would emerge from the sea riding a beast of the Apocalypse and charge at the soldier-guards, preferably those on duty at the southeastern watchtower.

Brave mustachioed — and not only — sergeants of the old era recount to astonished and trembling recruits that this Black Man had permanently vanished three or four sentries, and that around the post their weapons, cartridge cases, and boots were found, but not the slightest trace of the men themselves…

But the prisoners too have much to tell of the Black Man's appearances inside the isolation cell — especially those being punished — from which most emerged in wretched condition, bearing visible marks of their nightly struggle with the ghost.

What Mr. Floudas mentions in his communications has also been heard by this writer. Once, having gone to Rio to hear the brigand leader Skartsoras recount his life story, I heard there a multitude of legends about the disappearance of soldier-sentries and the appearance of the mysterious ghost of that most ancient fortress…
THE EXPERIMENTS OF THE SOCIETY
As Mr. Floudas announces, this matter was taken up by the Patras Society for Psychical Research at its session on January 17, 1933.
– We employed, Mr. Floudas continues, an excellent medium, the young woman S. G., who, after being placed in a hypnotic state inside the Rio fortress, began to speak in a trembling voice:
– I see a shadow. It does not look like a ghost… The shadow comes silently toward me… I am afraid… I want to leave… It is getting very dark…
– No, you will not leave, you are not afraid…
– Yes. I am not afraid, because now I see many great lights… They send out long flames, like fireworks… The flames are endless… and they all merge together.
– Ah… the flames have formed a Black Man… I am frightened… He is threatening me…
– Take me away!
– You will not leave. The Black Man is not harming you. You can ask him what he is and why he is there.

– Oh… Yes. I am not afraid. I am asking him… The flames you saw, he tells me, are the many people who labored to build the fortress… I am Diovahnesco, the master builder, and I am always here, because I like this place very much…

– I feel joy being in these places… Greater joy I feel when I see soldiers quartered here, for that was the purpose for which we built the fortress… I grieve deeply when I see prisoners and wish to punish them, for I want no prisons in my house — I want barracks.
No sooner had the medium said these words than it suddenly burst into screams of terror!
We could not restrain it, nor did it wish to tell us what it was seeing, and we woke it. We tried to repeat the experiment, but it proved impossible due to the medium's strong resistance.
THE MASTER BUILDER DIOVAHNENKO
In summary, Mr. Floudas states:

– We have established that the Rio fortress is indeed haunted, and the Black Man is none other than the master builder Diovahnesco — that is, his spirit, which, due to incomplete formation, appears and seeks vengeance upon those who converted into a prison what was originally intended as a military building.

It appears that this master builder died before the building was completed and, owing to the great longing he had in life to see the fortress finished, he appears and makes himself perceptible to people possessing particular psychic qualities.

The suggestion and autosuggestion practiced there — among soldiers in former times and among convicts — also contributed to the frequency and severity of the appearances of this ghost, this tormented spirit, the master builder Diovahnesco.

These events recounted by Mr. Floudas are a very small part of the multitude of truly supernatural phenomena proven by the research of spiritualism and psycho-philosophy. All these investigations and the most remarkable events established in the course of them will be recounted as we proceed.

First, many phenomena that appeared in ancient times and in various periods of history. Then we shall come to the scientific observations of spiritualism. And afterwards we shall recount spiritualistic phenomena that occurred in Greece from the time of the poet D. Solomos — who was a very powerful medium — up to our own days.
We shall also recount a host of the most curious and astounding phenomena that occurred throughout the world and are explained as communications of the dead with the living.
Fotos Giofyllis
ETHNIKI SIMAIA 25.01.1935

articles.title: The 65 Villagers of Naxos Speak with the Virgin Mary and Prophesy a Great War – 1935
articles.author: N. Kapitsoglou
articles.excerpt: Sixty-five villagers in Koronos, Naxos, fall into a hypnotic state and prophesy war, political uprisings, and the end of the world, claiming to speak with the Virgin Mary and saints.

image.alt: Koronos, Naxos – villagers and religious gatherings in the 1930s

content.value: The visionaries of Naxos, about whom we wrote a few days ago and concerning whom Mr. Tanagras of the Psychical Research Society ruled that they are simple villagers experiencing collective suggestion, are respected throughout the island and especially in Koronos, which is their home village.

There, all manner of people flock, either out of curiosity to learn interesting prophecies or out of interest in learning about their personal futures. Because this also happens. One visionary, as soon as he entered a state of suggestion, began to effortlessly grasp the thoughts of others and make predictions about their personal matters, exactly as happens with mediums. What is of greatest interest, however, is what the visionaries say about world affairs.

They say, quite simply, that war will very soon break out, and they know even details about how it will start and spread. Hungary and Yugoslavia — they envision — will initially be drawn into war, followed by most nations, not only in Europe but throughout the entire world. The suffering of the war will be unimaginable. The peace that will follow the catastrophic war, however, will be magnificent, ideal.

They further specify that the war will break out at the latest by the coming autumn. They also say that upheavals will occur in major European states before the war, and that major figures of global importance will leave this life as victims of assassination.

On this occasion, let it be noted as remarkable that three months before the assassination of Alexander of Yugoslavia, the visionaries had predicted — and it was even written in the newspapers — that a Balkan ruler would be assassinated in France. And since we are mentioning what the visionaries of Koronos, Naxos, have predicted over time, we must also add the following of their successes.

They had predicted the fall of the Venizelos Government as well as the coup of March 1st. Regarding the prediction of the March 1st coup, many long texts were written in the newspapers. It had been stated by the visionary Manolas, grandson of the first Manolas who had visions 100 years ago, here in Athens where he had come, as he claimed at the time, on the orders of the Virgin Mary on whose behalf he speaks.

Specifically, Manolas was led by the journalist of Akropolis to Mr. Tanagras, where, after making the sign of the cross and taking a deep breath, he sank into sleep — during which — for half an hour — speaking on behalf of the Virgin Mary, he said, among other things, about the coup of March 1st.

But the curious visionaries of Koronos do not only predict war. All of them without exception, from the first to the sixty-fifth, also predict a new movement in Greece, a Venizelo-Communist one, as they call it.

A movement which will last no more than three days and which will be suppressed by the army. They also predict that the King will come to Greece after war breaks out. As a conclusion, they speak of the end of the world. In exactly six centuries — as they claim — the Earth will be destroyed and the Second Coming will occur.

These and many other things are prophesied by the 65 villagers of Koronos — men, women, and children — during the hours when they sink into their strange sleep. Their fellow villagers believe that when the visionaries are in a hypnotic state, the Virgin Mary speaks to them, as does Saint John the Baptist and many other saints. They indeed claim, as the visionaries say with an altered voice, 'My son Jesus Christ commands' or 'My son God wishes' etc.

With these phenomena, all the competent authorities of Naxos have dealt from time to time, with the result that all concluded it is a matter of phenomena pertaining to psychical research. And indeed it is a psychic phenomenon. Those who have visions have been subjected to suggestion by previous visionaries who had themselves been subjected to suggestion. It is, in other words, a case of collective suggestion as Mr. Tanagras explains — who is in any case the most competent of all to explain the phenomenon — due to which the visionaries in this state also undergo religious delirium.

And he bases his opinion on the fact that as soon as one of the visionaries falls into a hypnotic state, the others fall one after another, and they are usually religious devotees and small children — people who are more easily influenced and subject to autosuggestion.

In any case, the phenomena do not cease to be of interest and to preoccupy the entire island of Naxos. As for the prophecies of the pious villagers, naturally no one can guarantee they will come true.
Author: N. Kapitsoglou
Source: AKROPOLIS 23.07.1935, p. 3

articles.author: Errikos
articles.excerpt: For a month, unknown stones strike a house every night in the Koufovouno neighborhood of Nea Ionia, Volos, causing fear, suspicions of a prank, and discussions of telekinetic phenomena.

image.alt: Koufovouno neighborhood, Nea Ionia, Volos in the 1950s

content.value: Whatever it may be — a prank or a telekinetic phenomenon — this stone-throwing that went on every night for a month in the Koufovouno settlement of Nea Ionia, Volos, described in publications by the local Volos newspapers, one thing is certain: the settlement needs to change its name.

Because a deaf mountain would be one where stones are hurled every night against Mrs. Siskos's house, making anything but a deaf noise, but rather disturbing all the people living there and deafening them with the tile-breaking.

By a curious coincidence, the precinct commander who was called to solve the mystery has the surname Kofos, and yet he heard the stone-bombs crashing into and breaking the tiles, but did not see who was quarreling with the tiles and pelting them.
The perpetrator was not, however, the legendary Kitsio's mother. Only her peers were considered suspects: Stella Kokkala and Tasia Vousvoura.
Whether they are the stone-throwers is uncertain, which is why the police who had arrested them set them free. And their names serve as justification of their innocence.
Can a Kokkala wage a stone war, and at night no less? She would freeze stiff at doing such a thing that crushes bones just like tiles.
And Vousvoura? At most she would spin around and not go saying she will grab a stone and hurl it to make Mrs. Siskos's and the neighbors' heads spin.
Could they be evil spirits? The terrified neighbors thought so and called the parish priest to exorcise them.
But at the very moment the exorcism was being performed, a cobblestone landed at the priest's feet. Meaning that even if they were demons, his presence had no effect on them.
Much incense was burnt on account of this affair from the neighbors' exorcisms.

Nevertheless, the customs agent living nearby, Mr. Ganotis, does not believe — as he declared — that these are supernatural apparitions, and thinks they are telekinetic phenomena, unless it is a prank, in which case the perpetrators deserve a proper polishing.
Author: Errikos
Source: Newspaper ANAGENNISIS 10.12.1953

articles.title: Souls of People Who Died in Athens and Elsewhere Appear in Corfu – 1939
articles.author: F.G.
articles.excerpt: Spiritualist sessions in Corfu are attributed to communication with souls of the dead from Athens and the provinces, with incidents causing intense concern.

image.alt: Spiritualist sessions and soul appearances in Corfu, 1939

content.value: The Most Curious Experiments of the Corfu Spiritualist Association
Spiritualist experiments always present exceptional interest. Many believe that in these experiments the souls of the living communicate with the souls of the dead.

The researchers of psychophysiology, however — such as Mr. Tanagras — do not believe in any communication with the dead and maintain that the so-called spiritualist phenomena occur through thought transmission between living persons or through other psychic influences.
Neither side convinces the other and so the matter remains unresolved. Meanwhile, however, new spiritualist phenomena are being observed.

In Corfu there has existed for approximately forty years the Spiritualist Association, which occupies itself with the so-called spiritualist phenomena and has conducted a multitude of experiments, at which many scientists and educated people have been present.
The medium is an educated young man who, whether hypnotized or awake, writes or speaks under a foreign influence, expressing what he sees or hears.
At this year's session of the Association, the medium suddenly fell to the floor and declared that he sees Saint Spyridon before him.

The president of the Corfu Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Mr. Efst. Agathos, recounts incidents in which the identity of spirits that appeared was verified, among them a man who died in Athens on Megalou Alexandrou Street.
The medium asked for the deceased's family to be notified. After investigation and corrections, the family was found and confirmed the details.
Another phenomenon concerns the appearance of the soul of an elderly woman from Zacharo, Olympia, with details verified from military records and relatives.
The spiritualists maintain it is a case of communication with the dead, while researchers of psychic phenomena attribute the incidents to suggestion and thought transmission.
But when those present at the session do not know the persons involved, how are the accurate details explained? The question remains unresolved.
Source: Newspaper Asyratos, 24.07.1939, p. 3

articles.title: Report to Police of Pursuit by Ghosts – 1933
articles.excerpt: A young woman reports to the 5th Police Station that she is being pursued by ghosts in her Athens home, with authorities and Angelos Tanagras examining hallucinations and telekinetic phenomena.

image.alt: Report of pursuit by ghosts in Athens, 1933

content.value: Athens, December 1st.

At the 5th Police Station there appeared yesterday in a distressed state a young and very charming woman, approximately 20 years old, Mrs. Evangelia Manta, and reported that she had abandoned her home at 35 Paparrigopoulos Street because she was being pursued by ghosts.

Her nervousness was not misinterpreted; on the contrary, it was considered natural given what she had experienced. The officer calmed her and asked her to return to her home with the assurance that ghosts would never trouble her again.
Initially, suspicion arose that, as is customary, some prankster was appearing as a ghost or had an interest in driving her from her home.

No such thing, however, was established. Since it was impossible for ghosts of hodjas and the Virgin Mary to appear before Mrs. Manta, as she herself reported, certain persons and things were appropriately examined.
It was established that the young lady had recently suffered a nervous breakdown, being in a state of separation from her husband, who is a mathematics teacher at the gymnasium of Pyrgos.
The talk of ghosts must be attributed to her nervous breakdown. Because of this, as Mr. Tanagras explained to us, she is suffering from hallucinations and believes she sees ghosts.
No other family had seen ghosts in the house where Mrs. Manta had been living until yesterday, and she went in terror to stay with a relative of hers in Piraeus.

Mrs. Manta also reported that on the same day she received strange disturbances from invisible forces and that, while standing before her mirror, she felt an icy breeze running through her body and ruffling her hair.
Terrified, she turned toward the exit and saw the bed covers lifting themselves up to a considerable height.
This phenomenon cannot be attributed to hallucination and appears to be a case of a telekinetic medium, as Mr. Tanagras explained.
The phenomenon of the icy breeze has also appeared with other telekinetic mediums as a precursor to telekinetic phenomena.
Source: Newspaper Ethnikos Kiryx, 18.12.1933, p. 2

articles.title: Ghost Boat Appears in the Saronic Gulf – 1934
articles.excerpt: Four fishermen of the Saronic Gulf claim that for four consecutive nights they saw a misty boat with women's voices and melodic songs, which sank each time they approached. Angelos Tanagras provides a scientific explanation.

image.alt: Archival image from the 1934 Apogevmatini newspaper article, p. 1

content.value: When the fishermen approach it sinks — they hear melodic songs coming from it.
A ghost boat appeared before astonished fishermen of the Saronic Gulf, precisely in the area between Fleves – Zoster – Cape Zervia.

Indeed, four fishermen claim that for four consecutive evenings, during the last dark nights before the new moon, they saw with their own eyes the ghost boat and heard coming from it enchanting melodic songs from sweet women's voices. But whenever they headed toward where the boat was, on all four evenings they saw it suddenly covered by a dark veil and then slowly disappear. Just as slowly the sweet melodic voice faded away.

Captain Giorgis Kosmidis with sailors Thoma Kasimatidis, Giannis Antipariotis, and Nik. Barkila felt the greatest emotion. All four swear that they saw with their own eyes the Ghost Boat and heard with their own ears songs from it, with a sweet woman's voice and then cries of pain and horror. The captain undertook to recount the details of the astounding phenomenon, stating beforehand that even now his hair stands on end merely thinking about it.
But before he began, we made the observation that they had not hurried to report what they had seen and heard to the police or harbor authority.
— And what if they had mocked us? he replied.

Now, however, since we convinced them that what they saw can also be explained scientifically, it is not impossible they will depose it to the Authorities, though it is now superfluous since it is coming to public light. With characteristic details at that.

— We were out at sea, the captain began, when we headed toward Lagonisi. We reached the strait between Fleves and Zoster, singing to pass the time. At a moment when we stopped to start another song, a woman's voice reached our ears. We all stopped breathing too. But what a voice that was! We all turned at once to see where it was coming from.

— A boat at Cape Zervia, Captain Giannis added. Indeed, it was a boat, gleaming, small. But how did it appear? Misty. As if wrapped in a veil, surrounded by haze. And yet the air was clear. The sea sparkled for miles. This struck us and we wondered.
— Good heavens, lads, what can that be?
And we headed straight for it. We all took up the oars and rowed hard. The song — words we could not understand — did not stop.
— What a song that was! Not even in Marseille and Alexandria in the cabarets did I hear the like, old Thoma interrupted.

— Straight to the boat, I cried, continued the captain. Imagine now our terror when we saw that the closer we got to the boat, the mistier its shape became, the more the sweet woman's voice faded. And suddenly — I say this and shudder — when we found ourselves two hundred meters away, the song stopped abruptly and the boat began to slowly sink. When it had completely disappeared, we heard clearly fierce male cries. Cries of agony, terror, and horror. Nothing of what they said was distinguishable. Our speech was cut off.
Without exchanging a word, as if on signal, we all began rowing in the opposite direction. One raised the foresail and we headed away. When we had gone far, we all said as one:
— A ghost, lads… Ghost Boat.
— All night, what mind had we for work? We talked of nothing but ghosts. When we returned to the small harbor, not a word did we say to anyone lest they start mocking us.
Everyone hung on the captain's lips as he recounted as if seeing before him this astounding phenomenon.

— The next evening, he continued, the same boat appeared again, the same songs and the same fierce cries we heard. This time, however, it passed by Cape Zervia and then behind us we saw the ghost boat and heard the enchanting song.

— After it, lads! I called out for us to approach quickly. But there was no stirring anyone. The song had paralyzed them. So this time we enjoyed the spectacle a bit longer. The misty boat. And we delighted in the song. We had lost ourselves there in the middle of the sea and it was the boat's disappearance that brought us back to our senses. Then came the terror — those fierce cries of the man.
I called out again for us to go to the spot where the boat had sunk. But no one wanted to.
We left then again for fishing and on the return took a course outside Fleves toward Faliro.

For the next night, however, we decided to reach the spot where we saw the boat. We even brought a revolver to shoot at it. Indeed, as soon as we saw the ghost boat again, we headed quickly toward it. I even fired twice at it. Nothing happened. Then, as on the two previous evenings, it disappeared slowly into the sea, while fierce male cries spread terror and horror. According to our plan, we reached where the boat had appeared, lowered the sail and rowed in circles. We saw nothing, however. Why then should we not accept that it was a ghost?

And he added: — Old Bias Kalaboka from Vouliagmeni told me well that he had seen the ghost boat. He thought it was his imagination. He had, however, told some educated people what he had seen and they told him it was truly a sea ghost.
— What do you believe? we asked the fishermen.
— Either that some shipwreck occurred there, or that some crime remained secret.

What can we add? Nothing more than the promise that we will go with the same fishermen to see the ghost boat ourselves. In the meantime, let us hear the opinion of a specialist, the president of the Society for Psychical Research, Mr. Ang. Tanagras, which is of considerable interest as he does not exclude the possibility that the fishermen truly did see the ghost boat.
Scientific Explanation of the Phenomenon
Here then is the explanation Mr. Tanagras gives.

— First, he told us, it may be a case of collective suggestion, transmitted by a powerful medium existing among the fishermen. This medium would suggest the exact scene that all the fishermen see, including the sounds.
And he cited as an example fakirs who suggest to their audiences even scenes of decapitating people.

The second explanation is that it has been observed for years that in places where violent deaths occurred, similar phenomena have often been observed — that is, a repetition of the scene of the violent death. In Greece too, similar phenomena have been noted from time to time. In these, all the scenes of the crime are repeated, having something automatic like a cinematic film. It should be noted that they recur when a powerful medium is nearby.
Regarding the Saronic Gulf phenomenon, Mr. Tanagras told us that it is not impossible that some crime occurred in that place whose scene is being replayed.

The most interesting of all is that the ghost boat can be photographed. And we have as an example a photograph of a similar phenomenon — a lady in white — in Austria, which was published in the 1929 volume of the Journal of Psychical Research.
We shall follow the phenomenon with interest and return to it in due course.
Source: Newspaper Apogevmatini 29.04.1934, p. 1

articles.title: Stone-throwing at Houses on Agia Triada Street, Vyronas – 1933
articles.excerpt: Mysterious stone-throwing targeting five or six houses on Vyronos Street in the Agia Triada neighborhood terrifies the residents, while the Police categorically deny any ghosts.

image.alt: Archival image from the 1933 Tharros newspaper article

content.value: In the Agia Triada neighborhood on Vyronos Street, mysterious and inexplicable things have been taking place for days, keeping the entire population of this large neighborhood of ours in agitation.

Five or six houses on Vyronos Street are being pelted with stones at midnight by invisible hands, and the residents are in a state of all-night turmoil. Despite all their efforts and investigations, it has proved impossible to discover the stone-throwers, and they are now convinced that the stones are being thrown by ghosts.
But should we really so readily accept that spirits and ghosts exist?

The matter is a bold one and only Mr. Tanagras and his followers can blindly believe in the existence and action of metaphysical forces. But then, what explanation must be given for these phenomena? I too do not know and am lost in various thoughts and speculations.

Since the stone-throwing is occurring on Vyronos Street, why should we not consider that we are being pelted by the spirit of our beloved Byron, as a sign of disapproval for the sorry state we have come to?

Another possibility is that these are not stones but meteorites, which as is well known fall by the millions in the month of August. Some of the neighborhood women, however, say they saw bricks among the stones. Others in turn say that one should look for the bricks among those who believe in these exotic phenomena.
Take your pick.

The Police Administration categorically denies what is being written — namely that on Vyronos Street, in one house, ghosts appeared and that police reinforcements were requested. No reinforcement was requested, nor did any ghosts appear. The ghosts appeared only in the imagination of the news writers, owing to the excessive heat.
Amyntas
Source: Newspaper Tharros 25.08.1933
